This game is a masterpiece, and every One Piece fan should definitely get it. For those who are yet not acquainted with the anime/manga it can work as a teaser of sorts, as the events from the original story are pretty well outlined, though you will get spoiled of course.
If you are unsure whether to get it or not, because you never played a dynasty warriors type game, don't worry. I had the same worries and that's the only reason I waited for sale. I now totally regret not getting it for the full price because it's just so worth it. It has become the longest single player game (apart from RPG games) that I played in my life. And I am still not done with it, so it may very well become my most played single player game of all time.
Great:
+Crazy number of playable characters
+Story mode and a super fun "wacky" mode with randomly generated levels
+Ridiculous number of collectibles, unlockables, progression
+Juicy, fluid, satisfactory combat
+Almost the whole story of One Piece (ends in Dressrosa, which has an original plot because I guess the manga did not conclude that arc when this game was released)
+Easy and accessible to everyone, but has some incredibly hard challenging difficulties which are unlockable for those who want a challenge - you can't really complain that it's too easy with the "super hard" difficulty for the story mode and the "nightmare log" version of the dream log mode.
Minor niggles:
-Your allies sometimes wander off somewhere and you have to rush to them to rescue them because them making it alive is sometimes required to succeed in a level.
-May be a bit grindy or too random with the "coins" needed to upgrade characters. Some coins require beating "strong enemies", there is like 20 of those, and it's completely random which one you will get. You may end up getting coins for 10 characters you were not that much interested in first.
Technical:
-Some people argue that the graphics are outdated, I don't really see that as a problem personally and I don't think it takes from the enjoyment of the game. I guess it is factual though. I've seen a guide on improving the textures here on steam though.
-Personally I had no problems with my xbox360 controller but some people have controller issues. Especially Xbox One controller seems to be broken right now, maybe there are fixes already, check the forums.
This game just rocks. It's a must buy for all One Piece gaming fans. I regret waiting so long to purchase it, but I am a very sensible customer and also a bit of a "budget" gamer, and I don't like blindly purchasing stuff for full price.
Buy it.
You won't regret it.

Preface, I know how this game was made, and what light, and I will not hold it to those standards.  I review from my own experience of the game, and will not set it into Pro or Anti feminist, simply a game.
PROS: The text adventure play of the console is a nice touch, adding some tension as the reactor has a meltdown.  The art is nicely down for the characters.  And...well, it's quick.
CONS: This visual novel has many failings.  The two female AI's are both rather unlikeable, both their actions beforehand and after.  They try to give a sympathetic reason to make their actions acceptable, but it fails.  The story is relatively dull, and the endings don't really feel satisfying.
ACHIEVEMENTS: Relatively simple, no real problems getting any of them.
FINAL: The visual novel's failings are it's major downfall.  Some could enjoy the more moe designs they try to go for, as well as the tsundere, but it's not something I will be returning to.

This was a plesant surprise in the field of world war 2 games on steam currently.  The story takes you through war-torn Poland, France, Norway, and Germany. You are an American reporter and help various members of each civilian's resistance against the German army.
The game suffers from a severe lack of difficulty even on the hardest option. Your character can stomach at least 5-7 mp40 bullets and while the health regeneration is slower than most other games, it's too easy to run away from any threats. The enimies's health also don't scale so if you're an experinced FPS player you can quickly down most of the enimies rather quickly.
That is the only serious problem aside from the occasional glitch which a quick checkpoint reset fixes.
The story is heart touching. I have a personal connection with the warsaw uprising and to just be a random guy and  they show it very well. While all of the German soilder's are Men, the Polish Home Army is made up of Men and Women in about a 3:1 ratio during the game. That was just a really nice touch to complete the desperation and show what people fought for during those 2 months.
Gameplay wise, there is a well done stealth mechanic. You have a meter on your hud and it'll make a noise and fill up red when you can be seen so you can quickly sprint and slide into cover to avoid being seen. You have a pair of binoculars so you can mark enimies and they'll have an yellow eye for a "passive" mode or  red for an "alert". You can see this icon through walls too. You can throw a rock to distract guards and they'll go on alert but won't siginal other soilders to the area.
The sniping mechanic is similar to the Sniper Elite games with the slow motion bullet cam and noise to cover sniper shots in a large area. The bullets seem to go off of the scope a little so it makes tight shots pretty difficult.
Each mission usually has a couple side missions which range from helping resistance members, blowing up tanks and halftracks, to releasing POW's from a prision camp.
Gunplay overall is satisfying even though it isn't innovaitve which it doesn't really need, the story and level design were the bigger focus. The game gives you a couple opprotunities to gun down Nazi's with a mg42 to satisfy your itch after slealthing past a group of them. There are also a decent number of slow-mo breaching sequences which are rather fun.
The level desgin in this game is amazing and really ties the game together. Your objective is in this village and on the opposite of the village is a river, you can sleath around the far outskirts of the town and get closer to your target. Very few times have i felt restrant on where a can and can't go. I may definitaly play through the game again and kill everything just so i can explore the levels because when you sleath through a level, you tend to only see the outside edge of half of it.
Playing through the game on expert and completing most of the side missions and playing with a mix of stealth and firefights. It took me a little under 7 hours to beat the game which is shorter than i would have liked to have experinced a lot more of the game but those hours were a solid 7 hours of good fun and a touching story.

So, this game has two entry barriers:
1) You should be willing to spend most of the time playing this game reading walls of text.
2) You should feel comfortable typing commands into a unix-ish kind of interface.
If these two things aren't instant turnoffs for you, you might like this game.
I don't really like games that are really "in-your-face" when dealing with certain topics. But, despite the lack of subtlety, this game really gets you thinking about its center topic (sexism) a lot, so I gave it a pass.
When it comes to mechanics, this game really knows how to create an immersive experience. Most of the things you see on the screen are diegetic so you might as well turn off the lights, put some headphones and pretend you are in the vicinity of a derelict spaceship, trying to learn its secrets through a computer terminal on a ship of your own.
The only thing that really bothered me, was that while using the terminal, I found myself pushing tab or the arrow keys the way as someone using UNIX or Linux would and though there's no real reason for the game to behave exactly as these systems it's kind of nice to have it respond to you the way you'd expect. It makes it for an easier and more comfortable interface.
Anyway, this game was a very interesting approach to visual novels and I really enjoyed playing it.

I’ve always been a sucker for new first person shooters. As long as you don’t go overboard on the paid content, free to play titles interest me as well.
Right from the start I was interested in Interstellar Marines. It wasn’t as if the small team was making yet another textbook example of an average FPS game. A lot of the mechanics are not commonly used in other games, and the environment is completely dynamic. Even the whole helmet idea seems “next-gen” (or whatever the marketing dept. is using these days).
Running off Unity, the game does quite well in the graphics department. While it is still not completely optimized, most systems shouldn’t have issues running this game.
COOP was introduced not too long ago, and there are several player vs. player gamemodes on offer. With such as small team, it is going to take a while to get to the actual meat of the game – fighting mutant sharks and what have you. I’ve seen an update every month, or close to.
Personally I wouldn’t recommend this game to everyone, but to those willing to wait it out, I’m going to recommend the game even in its early access state. As long as you are willing to wait out the slow release cycle, you should in theory have a very nice game to play. Yes there are going to be bugs, I’ve experienced a few in my playtime thus far. I have found that any bugs get addressed in the next update, so I don’t worry too much.

This is an excellent game.
Main premise: You are an industrial spy who wears a cool hat and a trenchcoat while trying to solve a murder (and make a killing in the meantime). You have two main abilities to help you do this (besides the hat): the BullFrog Jump Trousers which allow you to jump absurdly high distances and your Crosslink which allows you to hack into nearly any system, influding doors, security cameras, guns, trapdoors, and so on. The game requires you to master both of these abilities to be able to complete the brilliant puzzles it throws at you.
In case you didn't know this already, this is a puzzle game. The main point of the game is to solve puzzles by avoiding (or slaying) guards and hacking systems to acheive some objective.
Another fun element of the game is how much control you have over your character's morality. I personally tried to play the game without killing, hitting, or being seen by any guards, a feat I did not successfully accomplish. You can just as legitimately try to tackle every guard out of a window, however. There isn't that much of a different ending either way, but it was fun to try and solve the puzzles in so many different ways.
All in all, Gunpoint is a great puzzle game that I really enjoyed. My only critique is a relatively small one: the bug causing the game to crash on my computer unless I disable the Steam Overlay is a little irritating, especially because it keeps me from being able to play the Steam Workshop levels. Overall a great game, however. Keep 'em coming!

I was woefully ignorant of this game for many years, which is sad, because this is THE game I always imagined being able to play one day.
This is a game with such depth that it could only be an "indie" game. 3D rendering, fancy production, developer time-tables... all of that Big Name Developer stuff would make creating a game like this completely impossible.
UnReal World is a procedurally generated (yet large and persistent) world, inhabited by incredible A.I. There are numerous tasks always available for you to do, and the objective is simply to survive. But almost inevitably: you won't.
Your character struggles mostly against nature (and the occasional bandit or warrior). The weather, the ice, the BEARS. Go fishing, go hunting, go trading. Make tools and weapons and traps. Whatever you think you could do in an Iron-Age Scandinavian forest, you can do it in this game, with astonishing attention to detail and realism.
The animal A.I. is amazing. Wolves split and converge over long-distances with their packs, howling for communication. Kill the biggest reindeer in a pack (the leader) and the other reindeer will become aimless until they're picked off by other prey.
Combat, while not action-based, has a cold realism to it unlike anything I've seen. Your life isn't measured in "Hit points"... Rather your body, your limbs, your blood, your senses: they can all be attacked and taken away from you -- or you can take them away from your enemy. One hit in the right spot will debilitate you. Game over. But its a death that will make you smile. Dying is a part of nature, and a part of this game. Fight against it, but realize that its what makes your character's adventure... complete.
Hunting in this game is a challenge and never a guaranteed success. You, the player, as a person, need to learn the value of patience and deligence. But when you finally manage to track down your first elk or stag through vast reaches of forest, until at last the animal is too fatigued to run anymore... there is NO "kill" in a videogame I've found as satisfying as this. Yesterday I got really lucky, and chased a panicked reindeer that injured itself trying to scale down a cliff -- but when I finally caught up to it, a wolf had half-eaten its corpse, ruining the precious fur and making off with some of the meat.
Smoke/Dry the meat, tan the skin, feed your dog, and donate a cut of meat to the "gods" for letting you live another day. Work on building your cabin, or preparing the cold soil for future agriculture. There is so much to do, and it is all vital, well-designed, brilliant. This is a brilliant one-of-a-kind game that throws you into a real world like no other game I've ever played. There is no game I would more enthusiastically urge people to try. I am so happy this game has come to Steam, thus coming to my attention, and I have never been more happy to give a developer my money (thank you, Sami). Try this game.

I must admit that I like roguelikes and survival games and I like to try out many of them, I also frequently buy roguelikes on steam, but usually I play them for a couple of hours and then don't return to them. They might be interesting and fun, but only in few cases I really get hooked. I have played the steam version of URW for only 10 realtime hours (44 ingame days), but they flew by like nothing and I feel like I will  keep returning to this game.
Like with all games, I would only recommend the game if the setting appeals to you, which is based on stone age Finnland with all its harshness and mythology. Just watch the steam launch trailer, if it seems interesting to you, it might be worth buying this game. You have to be prepared to do some reading, there is a lot of ingame lore and many things you need to know in order to survive. The use of the online wiki is not required, there is a tutorial and an ingame encyclopedia, but still the wiki can be really helpful at times. Also, you will need to learn many keybindings and how to operate the game by keyboard. That is certainly not a game for the totally impatient, they won't survive long.
But that does not mean that the game is boring, there is a huge world waiting for you to be explored. And there is always something to do, there are different ways to keep your belly filled, as a hunter, fisher, farmer, trader and so on, but no matter which career(s) you choose, you won't be able to lean back. I haven't played a survival game yet which felt so realistic. I felt so happy when after few days of unsuccesful hunting, after many animals escaped me (despite following their track), and near starvation, for the first time I finally managed to kill a stag. I butchered it and cooked the pieces, which fed me for several days, until they got spoiled. I wasn't wise enough to smoke/dry them or to build a cellar for storage. I learned from it and my character became really promising, until I made the mistake to fight a couple of robbers, which led to an early death when I failed to treat my wounds. The game tells its own stories and even though the graphics seem horrible, the immersion is greater than in any other game I have played so far. I am looking forward to my next character and if he will be able to survive his first winter.
Tldr: In no other game I felt so happy and thankful to the gods of nature for being able to live another day.

Oh well, this "game" is more like a second job if you take it seriously.  Really, it can be so competitive that it's not even fun. Given time you can amass great power and influence.  On the other hand there are multiple activities that are fun by their own almost from the start, though most of them become boring through repetition.  Of course, the later isn't about blowing stuff - that's always fun.  The other side is that you can also be killed almost anytime and anywhere.  Speaking personally, not following a wise advice of "Don't fly what you can't afford to lose" made me stop playing twice already.  All in all Eve Online is best suited for focused people whose idea of leisure time is a switch of activity but at the same time it can easily break player's spirit when everything that he've spent countless hours on gets destroyed in mere minutes, sometimes even without any chance to predict or prevent that.  So, the immersion is very real life-like.

UnReal World is an engaging survival roguelike with an amazing amount of depth.
You're alone in the wilderness set in the iron age of finland. You create a character from scratch with tons of skills at your disposal. The player is given a lot of freedom and tools which grants a lot of variety. You can play vastly different and try various survival tactics in order to overcome nature and it's threats. Be a fisherman, farmer, hunter, gatherer or a bandit. You're given the choice.
The world itself is vast and filled with tons of items, creatures, immersion, lore and danger. It's very intricate and engaging with a great amount of detail. Every task that action that you perform has consequences and keeping your characters alive is really a challenge, furthermore the entire game is designed in a realistic way which only enhances the immersion. From fishing to hideworking or combat, everything is rough and has detail. It's a engrossing and hostile world.
A great aspect is the interactive story, despite not having a full blown campaign. You can chose from a variety of character backgrounds which vastly changes the start of your adventure. Start as a well equipped hunter or fisherman but if you're up for the challenge you can play as a runaway slave that is being hunted. You make your own story and it's done with such detail that you feel really immersed. Even though the minimalistic graphics aren't that advanced, the presentation is solid. The small amount of songs and sound effect will still grab your attention, as for the rest the text provides enough flavor to really make you feel like this lonesome adventurer. This is pretty much standard for most roguelike though but this theme really resonates with me compared to other dungeon crawlers.
The interface and controls are somewhat unintuitive but once you get used to it, it's really not that much of a deal. It might be a hassle at first to browse through the various menus but it's all set up in a reasonable fashion. That might be the biggest issue about this game, also there aren't many sound effects but it's still solid enough.
Overall this is a very lovely game and crafted with such dedication, if this type of game doesn't appeal to you. You will probably get frustrated and not really enjoy it. But if you do, you will be rewarded with a great survival game that actually makes you think about provide a good challenge, while having a strong theme with a realistic tone.
Definitely worth the price. Even if you're not sure about this game, you can still download it for free on the official website.

Not a full recommendation here for now, just wanted to share some thoughts. Some people might like it, others won't. I hope it does get some future updates with fixes for various stuff and complaints from the negative reviews. I'm keeping it positive.
So far im into Act1 right after we get everybody to the lifeguard station. It definitely looks much better(graphics and lighting wise) and more detailed, but it needs more work.
First my setup:
* FX-6100
* 2x4GB 1600MHz DDR3
* 2GB Radeon HD7850
* ProView with max res 1680x1050@60Hz
I did quite some testing around first 2-3 missions. Most of the time i was at "balance" preset in video seetings, vsync on. I had random fps drops also dropping to 30fps close and inside buildings and it was noticeable. Tinkering settings was not a fix for this. Instead i finally lowered res to 1440x900 and i started playing with 60fps on those same places it had drops to around 30. Not only that, but since its different resolution it has higher refresh rate and my fps went up to 75 on some places. I stayed at balanced and MSI Afterburner showed the card to be at 99% on the gpu and temps going toward 65 degrees C, around 1200MB video memory taken. CPU went up to 70% load. RAM - around 5000MB.
Some things i noticed:
* They changed the standart(good old) number plates on cars.
* Beach ball physics. Balls only roll for awhile when you walk into them.
* Weapon trunks don't spawn stuff right away when you exit and enter game again(no more exploits i guess?).
* Characters look better and more detailed.
* Characters move their face(lips) more when they are talking(or is it my imagination?).
* Game loading is shorter?
* Different music during loading for Act1(if i'm not mistaken it's from the jungle act).
* Ryder White is included, other dlcs should be.
* More stuff i or someone else is yet to discover(or already has :> ).
Ok, i admit i read about the first two and had to see for myself. Im not completely sure about the lips/audio sync yet. They might have changed other item physics as well. However I am sure it still needs some bug fixes. For now my biggest complaint is probably the blood fx on ground- textures are glitchy and look ugly like low res. Also the blood puddle when you kill a zombie has some strange mirror effect on the surface and looks horrible.
Using this new engine, DI is demanding. So what i would recommend if you have fps drops - find the right settings combo and most imortantly the right resolution to get higher and stable frame rates on your hardware.
Update 1: Only a few mission later...
* So far doesn't seem to be any desync between lips and audio.
* Objects/items placement is a bit off. Im talking about game objects, pickup items etc. For example on the way to the light house there is a crashed bus with luggage outside. The bags are slightly glitched(placed) in the bus. This is also noticed with some chocolate bars and wallets for example. Sometimes you have to change the angle and try again in order to pick them up. Nothing game breaking, but still worth to mention imo.
* Characters say additional lines, like when you drive through and successfuly kill a zombie.
* You can't enter the car from left side. In original DI there was a trick when you aim for the driver seat and when button prompt appears and you press it you immediately get in that seat. Just wanted to share this one :).
* Remember the mission where you have to put boxes and finish SOS sign otside the lighthouse. The places of the boxes are not white/transparent but rather blue-ish transparent. Ugh kind of hard to explain, but i think you get the picture. This is the same for all mission where you have to deliver something to e certain spot.
* I noticed new names of weapons: Awe inspiring home made machete. Never seen this kind of naming in the original DI, it must be new.
* Ragdoll physics are strange. When you kick dead bodies, you move them farther. While we are on topic about kicking, you know there are zombies which are dead by default, right? Sometimes when you kick them you get a "critical" hit sign. Weird.
Update 2:
* Jin looks kind of scary. There was some noise coming from the truck, yet neither she nor her father were working on it. I'm talking about the time when you enter the workshop and before you start mission to upgrade the truck.
* I was wrong about the weapon trunks/chests. But on some random occasions(i guess) there was no icon to open one or two just after i reloaded a game.
* Your character doesn't have a shadow. I am sure there was one in the original DI. You could see some weird 3rd person animations thanks to that :) .
* Some issues were fixed. Like the bunker where you take that russian guy from the helicopter crash. In DI there were shadows from the palm trees inside and the lighting was bad, like there was no ceiling. Nothing like that is presen in DI: DE.
* More new names i dont remember from DI - debilitating baseball bat, mediocre stick, worn heavy wrench, used military machete. You can correct me if im wrong about this, or anything at all.
* Ok, so the game switches back to windowed mode whenever it wants. I decided to try windowed with vsync off and at my max res 1680x1050. No framerate drops to 30. It runs better in windowed mode? Still takes a lot of juice from the card judging by the noise of the fans. Plays above 50-55 frames on balanced, in some areas above 60.
Update 3:
* It was hard to drive the armored truck in the first part of the island. The light was too bright. I don't remember being almost blinded before the upgrade. Maybe because of the armour thats taking half the windshield, i don't know.
* Aaaand some more new names like - enervating slicer. Ok, i think thats enough mentioning it.
* Perhaps i was a little rough when i talked about the blood fx, but i just dont like that puddle when you damage limbs/kill zombies. And the blood textures on some places on the ground don't look good and are flickering. Its like different textures are overlaping of some sort.
* Great weather fx in the city. It changes from sunny with clouds to dark and raining. Wow, the rain drops effect on roads and cars  is so cool and realistic.
* Crashed bus model in the city is updated and so is its interior. Changes like these affect placement of other objects like pickups(as i mentioned before). For example in one of the buses there is a chocolate bar floating in the air. Its close to the floor of the bus, but not placed on any surface.
Update 4: The more i dig in...
* Some of the NPCs seem slightly changed.
* Great fire fx. You can see this on crashed cars throughout the city that are burning.
* Loading really is shorter imo, but as soon as you enter the game the screen is a bit blurry and gets cleared in a couple of seconds.
* Someone mentioned that you can't see the base damage of a weapon when it's modified. I confirm it. Before you could see base damage + modified.
* Big baseball bat is now a cricket bat model, wtf. I didn't like it as a torch.
* Accepting missions has been changed. No more looking at a "piece of paper". Instead it is just a pop-up window on the left side. And your reward is no longer displayed.
* In the police station parking lot, the car before the door has open trunk. Inside the two bags are not properly placed or rather the car model has been changed without taking care of the details.
* They removed or moved some of the weapon mods. There was one for sharp weapons on the table right outside the police station. It's gone now. I haven't found it yet.
So, the more i dig in... is it worth it? I'd recommend this for fans and only on sale. It has updated visuals, lighting and effects. A bit heavy on the gpu depending on your setup. Developers might have addressed some issues and missed a lot more caused by this "upgrade". They changed stuff that didn't need to be. Feels like it's rushed and needed more testing.

First of all I bought this during Summer Sale 2016 so I got it really cheap (72 Rupees or about $1.5), and what can I say...I definitely got more than my money's worth. And I only just completed the Single-Player campaign so far (was a 7-hour affair for me). When I was buying this game I thought I was in for something like a CoD: World at War remastered with some Commandos: Strike Force DNA thrown in - and that's exactly what I got. What I didn't expect was the bit of Sniper Elite DNA that I got along with it.
GRAPHICS - Good! Although it certainly seems the devs did not make full use of the CryEngine's capabilities, and some bad textures here and there, it definitely succeeds in refreshing the WW2 FPS genre with such much-needed graphical upgrades. But mind you, for 2016 standards you might just be left wanting a BIT more!
ANIMATIONS - Can do with a lot of improvements. Facial animations are not really good at all...and even the reloading and opening/closing doors animations seem blocky.
STORY - Nothing too captivating or "out there" about the story itself...while avoiding any spoilers, I will say it does suceed in highlighting the efforts of the Resistance fighters in WW2. Not many games out there that do this - usually you're with the Marines or the Red Army but not in this game (although if you look at the protagonist's supposed occupation as a war-reporter and look at the kind of stunts he pulls off...maybe he's better off joining SAS or something).
What does deserve a special mention though is the variety of environments where you play...and how well the look and feel of each level has been executed. I've always loved looking at the distant objects/backgrounds in game levels (mountains, sky etc.) and this game has satisfied me well in that regard. See my screenshot uploads for this game to understand what I mean.
GAMEPLAY - Your run-of-the-mill FPS mechanics. Nothing new or revolutionary here...but what the game does execute, it executes rather well. Especially the shooting part - aiming down the sights of a silenced SMG and dispatching patrols has not felt quite as good in many other games. The stealth aspect is something I have not yet fully explored (I'm sure I blazed my way through many areas that I'm sure I could have passed with silenced weapons and minimal killing) - and the minimap is simple but extremely helpful, as is the 'tagging' mechanic.
You don't get to do any driving or anything so that's a little disappointment (throughout the game I was expecting atleast a minute-long drive-by sequence...but it didn't happen), but yeah well the driving in an FPS title is likely to suck anyway so I guess I haven't lost out on much.
I would have preferred it if they implemeted some sort of a scoreboard or something at the end of a mission to show how you did (or how you could have done better) but there's no such thing.
Final verdict? You are getting a solid 7 to 8-hr campaign (haven't tried the MP yet, mind you) that pretty much delivers all that it promises. If you played other WW2 FPS titles before...believe me you'll get a lot of throwbacks and might just be hit by a wall of nostalgia at some point. You are unlikely to be all that surprised at what this game offers...but you won't regret buying it either. RECOMMENDED!

Got it as a gift from a friend. Best! Gift! EVER! I love this game to
, bits of ice stages, bits of my enemies, bits of myself and beat of the spooky tracks during the awesomely designed bossfights that actually depend on skill of all players and can range from lame and easy to awesomely difficult!
Seriously, if you're a fan of stickmen(little reason to come here otherwise) and a fan of frantic 4-player fighting with whacky physics, exotic weapons, player bosses, a bucket of skill and a smudge of ol' random, I can't recommend this enough. The fun value(screw the hours) is immense unless you're a sore loser; Winter, Western, Lava and Halloween levels are beyond awesome; sneks are cool even when you're being chomped yourself; rounds are quick and fun, especially on destructible(Winter(ice), some Lava(platforms on chains)) and movable(Western(some levels are made of boxes)) levels.
Now, don't get me wrong, this game has its downsides, the biggest is the bad netcode that can't sync up everyone for the life of it, most of the time everyone's only roughly where they actually are, and gods help you when you're on the receiving end of the big and killy desync choppa. First time I played it everyone was standing still for about first 10 seconds of every round, then SUDDENLY action, and after those 10 seconds I usually ended up either one hit from dead or already dead. Was kinda fun, but not as fun as it could've been.
Today I was fine, so maybe it was a 1st launch thing. Some people are still poorly synced up, but it's perfectly fine on my side. Was accused of cheating multiple times by a guy that somehow got himself lag-teleported in between two big boxes that are holding a platform, t' was a good session.
The game can be competitive if you want it to be btw, private lobbies are a thing, just gotta make sure that everyone's synced up and then you can beat the crap out of each other with even more skill involved than on average!
So, overall? I'd say it's somewhere around 7/10, because sync problems are a major issue, offset only by how well-designed and fun the game is in its simplicity.

First things first; if you own the original Dead Island on PC you can get this for $3 US. It is definitely worth it at that price.
However if you didn't like the game in your experience, this will not change your mind. This is admittedly a chance to get the game on the newer consoles and Deep Silver took it. I believe there is only a PC port as a thank you to Dead Island fans (hence the $3 loyalty price). Well, to Deep Silver, I say you're welcome.
The game plays about the same, which may or may not bother most people to insanity, but it looks a lot better than the original game and I am pleased with the graphical upgrade personally. It admittedly could have looked a lot better, but doing a game over as opposed to re-developing it from scratch probably cut a lot of the development time.
It really comes down whether you like the game at all. I think a lot of people on here bashing it or saying it isn't worth even $3 to get the new version didn't like the game to begin with. If you do like Dead Island and/or Dead Island: Riptide (flaws and all), then this definitely worth a purchase in my opinion.

Half-Life 2, and its episodic sequels, are examples of the pinnacle of story-driven gaming. Sure, they're all incredibly linear games, but they're so perfectly linear and captivating, almost to the point of perfection. Their stories flow from scene to scene, taking the player on a wild ride that, just like a good book, they just can't put down.
Estranged is not Half-Life 2.
It uses the same design principles, is builty on the same engine, and apart from the story could even be described as the same game. However, the story of Estranged fails to capture its audience and get them interested from the start, by using the cliche of "guy becomes shipwrecked on a mysterious island". It also moves quite slowly, with the only real action emerging in the last third of its 120-odd minutes of gameplay. Just as in Half-Life 2, the gameplay is lacklustre, so the story must pick up the slack and keep the audience interested, which it fails to do.
That said, there are some interesting sequences which may yet save this game. Creeping through a warehouse expecting to find zombies (yes, there are zombies) was tense, and the ability to view the desktops of some virtual computers give some hints as to what the story is about. All that, and taking into account that this is only Act 1 with more to follow, tip the scales slightly in favour of me recommending it. Also, it's free, which is good because you wouldn't want to pay money for this. So for now, I'll give Estranged the benefit of the doubt, but if Act 2 fails to capture my interest then I will probably give up on the series entirely.

Eve Online, a game where you believe at first it is quite dull and absolutely not entertaining. A game that from a modern perspective appears like it's stuck in time. Granted, it's old and definitely not a new game, but a game I can whole heartedly recommend.
Before I begin with my recommendation however, I'll tell you the biggest downfall of this game. It's a game where you pay a subscription. Now, this is not a problem for most people, but I am not that financially stable and have tried my best to play this game for 5 years whenever I could squeeze in the money. If that doesn't show dedication, I don't know what will.
To begin with, this is a sandbox. This game gives the community the entire freedom to do as they choose with, at least when it comes to all areas on the map that are considered "null-security", meaning no NPC protection, no laws, nothing. You make the rules.
There are elements given by the developers, like mission running, killing enemy pirates, mining asteroids, gas or ice, battling other players, diplomacy and politics and more. These elements are often not that entertaining on their own, such as for example killing pirates. The game mechanics require not too much input from your side, but don't be deluded about this fact. This is all just a hoax to hide the real game!
Because the real game is nothing what you originally expected. You thought looking at pretty lasers while pressing your modules was the game? Wrong. You thought spending hours on end trying to increase your money was the game? Wrong. You thought spending hours to elevate your skills to fly better ships was the game? Wrong.
This is real life. Now, I don't mean that this will replace your real life, or it might! However, truly, this game is all about the players. Exploit, create, procrastinate, destroy, betray, befriend, bewilder, bestow, abolish, subjugate and idolize. The players are the game and what you make with them. Do you want to control an entire area in space? Do you want to be the powerful military strategist? Do you want to be a General, commanding hundreds of players to their capsuleer death? Do you want to be the spy, that infiltrates the enemy and destroys them from within? Do you want to be a politician everybody likes and rise to power? Do you want to be the most influential industrial player, that produces exactly what everyone desires? Do you want to be a hero? A villian? The story is yours! Truly yours!
In this game, you create your own gameplay, you create your own story and you find your own path. Do not trust anyone! Trust is your most valueable asset, don't give it away for cheap or you might find yourself with a steak knife in your eye-socket, or in this case, in your carrier. Don't be afraid by the hard learning curve this game delivers, because it will, but it is so worth it. This game has so much more content than people often realize and the world is so much bigger than you!
You can become anyone and anything in Eve Online, granted if you can afford the subscription! But now it's free to play, although very limited, but at least you can enjoy everything you can do with players and who knows, maybe you can use that to your advantage and convince players to pay for your subscription through ingame currency? Yes, that's a thing ;)
If you've ever wanted to see how humanity works, how it ticks and wanted to be somebody special, somebody meaningful and didn't like the 50 years wait in real life, in eve, you'll only have to wait a year or two to learn the game and skill and you're right there, in your own story and don't you worry for a moment! Eve history is recorded, yes, literally recorded by actual players who write up eve history and news. Remember, all news, just like in real life is biased! But read it anyway and make up your own mind!
There are fansites, places to learn, universities(yes, really!), a great community and devistating realities like losing everything you possess. If you've ever wanted a game where you can become anything and lose everything without the worry of death, this is your treat.
Enjoy the ride of this fantastic game and fly safe! o/
PS: If you need any help, you can find me ingame. Contact "Kevin Snow". :)

At the start of the game if you just jump right into a quick match against the computer AI, you don't really know what to do. You can't highlight (like in most RTS games) over your vehicles/fleet that you control, it's mostly a right click RTS game (via the mini-map). You right click to send your vehicles somewhere to take over a base, production line, etc then you right click again to move them to a different area. You can of course put these vehicles into groups so that you can control them better, but that is still hard to do when you can't highlight over the vehicles as I stated. Once you get past the whole right click, the game is actually fun to play.
Gameplay/graphics wise, the game runs and looks great for a 2012 published game. For those who want more out of the game, there is a single player campaign in which you can dive deeper in the storyline (which I haven't). If you play a quick match against the AI in gamemodes like Sabotage, the computer will always have nukes. The nuke has a huge blast radius in which it can destroy your whole fleet of vehicles if it's in that area (even out of the red circle vehicles can get damaged). Having the AI with the nuke 24/7 makes the gamemodes kinda boring, but more or less kinda intense since you always have to predict where the AI will put the nuke down. If you have enough skill points, you as well can get the skill trait of using nuke but that will take some time.
For $8, it's a fun game to waste time.

It has certainly been a while since i played this game and want to say my PTSD has dropped so i guess i might as well review the game. Oh dear god no. Well i am reviewing the game in a pro / con style and ending the game with my conclusion. I want to warn you that i am review the game in 2016 not based on when it came out. You have been warned.
Pro:
The guns sound pretty cool. I really enjoy the sound of jacob snipers mainly since i played as the sniper dude primarily. Yes i really dont know how to spell his name so i am calling him the sniper dude. Regardless firing the guns felt like a treat with how the guns sound. The guns simply had a charming sound i like.
Each character you choose has their own abilities and unique perks the player could choose from. This helps separate the different play styles that can be obtained with each character such as running in killing everyone with your fists or hanging back and picking people off with your sniper.
The guns leveled up the more you used them, that was pretty cool to see that me killing enemies was worth something more than just exp and money. Now my accuracy with a sniper is even higher or i do more damage with headshot or whatever. It felt that every kill i did ment something more.
Con:
Is there a story? That is a legit question since i honestly do not know. Pretty much the game progression is mission based where you dont necessarily get plot related exposition. When i played through the game it felt that i am just doing missions and not progressing any story what so ever. I want to say you do like five or seven mission till you get to some major plot related part where you get a vault peice and then the game slows back down and that means more missions that feel there for padding. If we take out all the padding i think the game would last for like one and a half hours long.
Wall of text when accepting a mission. I dont know if this is how they explain the story or what not but no one has the time to read something that is more than a few sentences long. It kills the pacing of the game to finish killing a ton of enemies to be greeted by a large ammount of text probably used a exposition..
The wasteland is boring. What killed me more than the feeling of lack of progression is being in the wasteland for about 99% of the game. It is brown really makes me tired. I enjoy seeing more locations rather than strictly wasteland.
Was there music? Well i dont know because i turned it off after my playthrough. None of the music really stood out to me as entertaining or gave me a feeling of a cohesive atmosphere. So yea music is a negative.
Dlc was it great? Well it did add more to the story but struggled being all around interesting. Alot of bosses were just too much for one person soloing who is a sniper character. The zombie island one I will give a like since it has zombies and i certainly do enjoy a good zombie experience. Not that it was great but was something to do, slaughtering undead. Other dlc i can sum up as just meh.
Moxxies underdome....Yea that dlc is just horrible. Your in this survival mode where you kill wave on wave of enemies. Ok but that is not all says the game. You must also survive the buffs or debuffs that the player or enemies experience on every round. Now i roll my eyes in annoyance but that is not all says the game. You must survive 5 rounds made up of 5 waves each round which means a total of 25 waves. Now i slam my head against my desk but that is not all says the game. After doing that for each of the 3 respective arena's you can do it all over again but this time you will have 20 or 25 rounds made up of 5 waves per round. At this point i turn off the game to prevent the game from saying but wait there is more to this dlc. It has not story soooo why is it even here? It isnt even fun, it is a misserable chore to do.
Fires a shot from a powerful gun and get no hit even when i am aiming right at the enemy. Yea there is this nasty little issue where sometimes your bullets dont count. You fire a shot and you know you hit them but the game is like hahaha no you didnt and you just wasted some useful ammo for your most powerful gun.
Fires a shot from a powerful gun and get a damage counter of 0. I am not joking with this. It is similar to the issue just above but this time i get an indication i hit them and the damage i see is 0. I am a higher level than the enemy and using a higher level gun but still manage to get a damage output of 0.
Conclusion:
This game was just too much for me to do. After i got my 100% list i was done and took a break from it. I should of done a review earlier but had PTSD from the game. I can not recommend the game for 2 reasons. 1 all the issues i pointed out in my list. 2 if you get borderlands 2; it has a story and gives a really brief segment about what happened in borderlands 1. So with that you can skip the game entirely and not be confused about the sequal. Again this game probably was good way back then but now it just is not, i recommend borderlands 2 over this because it is in everyway better. Good to see the developers took peieces of this game and made a master peice with it's sequal.

It's a good game. Fast-paced "Warriors-like" game heavily influenced by the world of One Piece.

First of all, know that you will spend most of your time reading plain text without pretty images in this game. This is by no means a game for everyone, but if you like reading books that do not shy away from heavy subjects and social issues, this is probably a game for you.
This story explores a real period of history with extreme gender inequality, but puts it in a science fiction setting. The start is a little hard to get into, but soon enough a highly compelling mystery story emerges, touching on topics as surpression, marital problems, abuse, forbidden love, and having to adapt to a society that is not your own. It is not pretty and some parts may be hard to read, but the interpersonal, psychological, and sociological aspects of it are very deep and realistic, and the pieces of the story come together in a horrifying yet unique and captivating way.
If all of that sounds interesting to you, I highly recommend playing/reading this interactive novel.
Also, be prepared that due to "technical issues" in the computer system of the space ship Mugunghwa, the AI will at times force you to give overly black and white answers to questions that really need a third option. When that happens, remember that in the story your possible answers are formulated by the AI, and as such are colored by their own way of thinking, not that of the protagonist.

I'm an old gamer. I used to play classics like Cultures back in the day and loved it. Recently I was looking around for something to scratch the "Colony sim" itch while expanding on the idea. Then I remembered I wishlisted Rimworld hoping it would go on sale, but it never did. So I finally said screw it and grabbed anyway. I'm now 17.7 hours in over 2 or 3 days and completely hooked.
This game is incredible. Its one of those magical games where its 10a.m. and you decide to play a bit, then its 11p.m. and you conclude the game is the missing link for time travel. Rimworld is often described as "deep" because of all the small details it provides about everything in the game, living or non-living, but instead of deep I would rather use a word like "entertaining". You see, almost every aspect of the game is randomly generated, but it does so well enough that everything fits together well enough to be immersed. As your game progresses, your management choices cause ripples in the minds of your colonists and their lives, making for great drama if your tv is out. You can see plenty of crazy Rimworld stories around, and the best part is that these stories are the norm. You don't have to do anything special to find the interesting stories, they just happen.
I read some of the past updates, and it seems that the storytelling gets more and more facets with every update, and at this point its in that golden point where its still got that early access pricetag but its so close to release that you might as well be getting it on sale. I highly recommend it, as it has stuff for both the zen strategist and the in-the-moment Sims player.

Summary: It's a fun(ish) game with lots of flaws. Only buy it on sale ($5 or less)
Double asterisks ** indicate that that aspect has a relevant pro/con to accompany it.
Pros:
-I bought it for $2.99**
-Sometimes the graphics look good, has beautiful scenery**
-Sounds are usually good**
-If you crouch and focus on a target long enough to get a red circle with a sniper rifle, it imitates Sniper Elite slomo kills (without the detailed penetration).
-Has cool cinematic scenes that move around a frozen 3D environment before levels. Cutscenes have effective cinematography.**
-Offers "stealth" approach**
Cons:
-I bought it**
-Some textures are high res, some are low res and blurry**
-High contrast visuals are harsh on the eyes, cannot adjust in-game**
-Sometimes the sounds of guns drop or dont play properly, occasionally one or two shots are un-synced**
-Shots sometimes "miss" in spite of having been aimed properly.
-Acting isn't always great, it has its moments but not enough of them.
-"Cinematic" scenes are all played at a poor resolution and appear blurry compared to the game.
-Grass, and other such textures are flat textures and their use as cover varies from usable to nonexistent (again the game fails to remain consistent).
-Stealth is poorly implemented and is pretty much unusable, not only due to the stealth interaction scenes appearing sluggish/slowed down and therefore looking ridiculous, but also because there are not enough opportunities to effectively use stealth.**
-Movement has a slidey effect which I got used to after a short while, but it is ridiculous and annoying nonetheless.
I'm sure there are more cons but you get the idea, the game is vastly flawed and is really only worth $3-5. The game description claims to be non-linear FPS but due to poor implementation of stealth and sabotage and the lack of silenced snipers (at least 2 hrs into the game) sniping is also only effective in combination with the use of other weapons and finally finishing off the last few enemies with CQ combat as they tend to hide and not come out sometimes. I only recommend it if you get it on sale, have an afternoon to kill, and don't mind not being able to use half of the game mechanics (stealth, "sabotage", etc.) due to poor implementation.

There is also online mode, but I haven't checked that out (might be dead or not).

Eve Online, a game where you believe at first it is quite dull and absolutely not entertaining. A game that from a modern perspective appears like it's stuck in time. Granted, it's old and definitely not a new game, but a game I can whole heartedly recommend.
Before I begin with my recommendation however, I'll tell you the biggest downfall of this game. It's a game where you pay a subscription. Now, this is not a problem for most people, but I am not that financially stable and have tried my best to play this game for 5 years whenever I could squeeze in the money. If that doesn't show dedication, I don't know what will.
To begin with, this is a sandbox. This game gives the community the entire freedom to do as they choose with, at least when it comes to all areas on the map that are considered "null-security", meaning no NPC protection, no laws, nothing. You make the rules.
There are elements given by the developers, like mission running, killing enemy pirates, mining asteroids, gas or ice, battling other players, diplomacy and politics and more. These elements are often not that entertaining on their own, such as for example killing pirates. The game mechanics require not too much input from your side, but don't be deluded about this fact. This is all just a hoax to hide the real game!
Because the real game is nothing what you originally expected. You thought looking at pretty lasers while pressing your modules was the game? Wrong. You thought spending hours on end trying to increase your money was the game? Wrong. You thought spending hours to elevate your skills to fly better ships was the game? Wrong.
This is real life. Now, I don't mean that this will replace your real life, or it might! However, truly, this game is all about the players. Exploit, create, procrastinate, destroy, betray, befriend, bewilder, bestow, abolish, subjugate and idolize. The players are the game and what you make with them. Do you want to control an entire area in space? Do you want to be the powerful military strategist? Do you want to be a General, commanding hundreds of players to their capsuleer death? Do you want to be the spy, that infiltrates the enemy and destroys them from within? Do you want to be a politician everybody likes and rise to power? Do you want to be the most influential industrial player, that produces exactly what everyone desires? Do you want to be a hero? A villian? The story is yours! Truly yours!
In this game, you create your own gameplay, you create your own story and you find your own path. Do not trust anyone! Trust is your most valueable asset, don't give it away for cheap or you might find yourself with a steak knife in your eye-socket, or in this case, in your carrier. Don't be afraid by the hard learning curve this game delivers, because it will, but it is so worth it. This game has so much more content than people often realize and the world is so much bigger than you!
You can become anyone and anything in Eve Online, granted if you can afford the subscription! But now it's free to play, although very limited, but at least you can enjoy everything you can do with players and who knows, maybe you can use that to your advantage and convince players to pay for your subscription through ingame currency? Yes, that's a thing ;)
If you've ever wanted to see how humanity works, how it ticks and wanted to be somebody special, somebody meaningful and didn't like the 50 years wait in real life, in eve, you'll only have to wait a year or two to learn the game and skill and you're right there, in your own story and don't you worry for a moment! Eve history is recorded, yes, literally recorded by actual players who write up eve history and news. Remember, all news, just like in real life is biased! But read it anyway and make up your own mind!
There are fansites, places to learn, universities(yes, really!), a great community and devistating realities like losing everything you possess. If you've ever wanted a game where you can become anything and lose everything without the worry of death, this is your treat.
Enjoy the ride of this fantastic game and fly safe! o/
PS: If you need any help, you can find me ingame. Contact "Kevin Snow". :)

If Dwarf Fortress interested you but your bounced off the complexity and the learning curve of that game then this game might interest you. There is a free version the creators website, but it is an older version. The latest version on steam has a revamped graphics and new features. The new graphical upgrade does look better. You can zoom out and see much further or zoom in close to your character. This game may not have eye candy graphics but its gameplay pulls you in. Its a survivalist game where the details can kill you. You have to think about what you are going to do next, based on your characters condition and the environment, how much food you have, fatigue and sleep etc. Merely eating any food wont in the long run do you any good if you stick to fish for example because your nutrition will suffer, which means you get fatigued faster. You can trap, track and hunt game. But its not easy, often they get away, but some game are easier to catch than others like squirrels for example. One time i was nearly straving and came back to my camp before it got dark and discovered one of my small deadfall traps had my dinner. There are aspects of the game i havent delved into yet, such as owning a dog which can help out with hunting. The game is turn based, but you can still get into trouble with burning your food if you go off and do a long consuming task or sleep, or you can have your food spoil if you do not eat it in a reasonable time or preserve it. There are NPC in the game whom you can trade with to get better quality gear which makes doing tasks much faster eg. chopping down trees with an iron axe instead of a stone axe. There is many skills you can invest into and level up. Some other features in the pipeline sound interesting, such as being able to marry and have offsrping which when your character dies you can resume as one of your offspring.  This game has more potential to come in the future. The game does lack music and sfx, there is some but could be more. But that really isnt important with the depth this game has under the hood.

Day of Defeat: Source is an awesome first person shooter inspired by WWII. There are classes, two gamemodes, achievements, and maps!
Choose to be a rifleman, assault class, support class, sniper, machine gunner, or rocketeer. Riflemen are capable of using their semi-automatic M1 Garand (U.S. Soldier RIfle) to take down enemies from long distances and with two hits while the german variant has a bolt action one that does more damage. Assaults can smoke enemy positions and charge in there to destroy the enemy team. The support class is for covering fire and is pretty versatile. Has a medium damage and ranged weapon with two frag grenades/potato grenades. Snipers are self-explanatory. They have a sniper rifle for shooting people at long distances. Machine gunners are more of a defensive class. They can place a machine gun while prone or on a sandbag and mow down an entire team although they're vulnerable. Rocketeers are for picking off key targets most likely machine gunners and snipers and have rocket launchers. They also come with sidearms. The U.S. Army rocketeer has a quick firing M1 Carbine while the German rocketeer has a close quarters C96 machine pistol.
There are two gamemodes for you to play. You have territorial control and detonation. Territorial control is a gamemode where you capture flags around the area. There are usually 5 flags with each team holding 2 and one middle flag uncapped. This is the typical, main gamemode in Day of Defeat: Source. Detonation involves detonating explosives at an opposing checkpoint and sometimes uses an offense vs. defense setup.
It's not the easy game to just pick up and be good at, but it's a fun game.

Oil Rush is a bland and repetitive RTS game where you do not actually control individual units, but control groups of units that are produced from pre-placed production buildings which both sides are fighting for. All you do is fight for control points that either create units or produces oil for towers or upgrades. You can only command 25%, 50% or 100% of units around a certain control point and then you send them from control point A to B. Hands down one of the best roguelikes I've ever played. Played the free version on and off in the past before buying it on Steam to show my modest support and appreciation for the Devs.
Being developed and consistently updated for over 20 years, Unreal World is set in a world resembling ancient Finland in the Iron Age. The gameplay has a ton of freedom and depth, and the setting is rich in its historical atmosphere and lore.
There are many ways to play, you could be a farmer, hunter, a gatherer, a fisherman, a adventurer or trader as you find your path in this harsh, gritty world. There are no set rules, you decide where to go and what to do. Despite the simple graphics the gameplay is very realistic. It takes creativity and experience to accomplish some of the harder tasks like hunting. You really feel like you're part of the world as you make your way through the four seasons every year.
The game has its roots as a ASCII-based roguelike. If you've never played one of those before it might seem daunting to learn the controls, since for these games there're a lot of commands, akin to playing a flight simulator on the keyboard. It honestly isn't too hard to learn, and the in-game help browser and beginner game course is actually very helpful. If you don't mind learning the controls or if you're already a roguelike enthusiast like me, I highly recommend giving it a try.

After watching Totalbiscuit's quick look at Oil Rush the development descisions start to make more sense. Check out his video on youtube for an accurate description of what the game is like.
Pros:
- Great graphics
- Interesting mix of strategy and tower defense
Cons:
- Cheesy, imbalanced, repetitive campaign
- Not much variety, one race/set of units for everyone
Rating:
2/5
So Oil Rush is a game created by a Russian company called Unigine Corp specifically to promote their engine coinsidentally named Unigine. Promote the engine it certainly does as it's a beautiful game to look at. As for the gameplay, Oil Rush is lacking.
First some things I did like about the game. The graphics I already mentioned are great. The water effects and texture detail stand out as being very good for a smaller engine like this. The music is decently catchy but the quality is poor.
Probably the best part of the game is the interesting mix of strategy and tower defense in an uncommon way. In Oil Rush you don't base build, you capture bases (zones, if you will) that spawn specific types of units or provide you with resources. You also don't control your units individually but rather as a group and send them off to attack and capture. Killing enemies also gets you command points you can use on upgrades. They're all very straightforward but they again add just a bit of variety to make the game more interesting. You use the resources you collect to surround your bases with towers preventing an easy capture when your forces are away or on some of the command point powers.
At first this all looked straightforward and a bit boring to me but after playing with the mechanics for a few hours against a hard AI, the system actually does provide for some very tense fights and strategy in which bases you fight harder over to get the units you want and how you split the forces you do have to cover several sides of the map. After awhile you're thankful you don't need to control individual units so you can focus on the map as a whole. This isn't an entirely new idea for a game, building up forces until you have superior numbers and capturing nodes I've seen before but Oil Rush does do it with just a little bit of spice to keep it interesting.
-------------------------
Now for some of the bad parts of the game. It's cheesy and it shows, especially in the terribly voice acted campaign. I couldn't actually test the multiplayer since of course the game is deader than dead by now so I was restricted to the campaign and AI skirmishes. The campaign follows a very linear story arc, which is fine for a strategy game if the missions were fun but in this case they're really not. Several of the missions are artificially difficult with enemy units 'magically' appearing out of the side of the map and attacking your weakest base the very second you leave it.
Other missions mix up the game completely and turn it entirely into a tower defense game with you controlling platforms that only allow turrets to be built while you watch enemies slowly move along a set path through them. If these levels were good it'd be a welcome addition to mix up the pace but they're not. There's none of the tenseness of a tower defense, none of the mayhem or strategy, you can literally spam any tower you want and win these levels UNTIL the last wave or so when they throw super enemies at you which you aren't ready for since the last 19 waves had nothing like that. That's the kind of stuff that makes those levels more frustrating than fun. Overall it's not an entirely terrible campaign, just tedious and uninteresting enough that I certainly wouldn't want to play it more than once.
Also to note is there's only one race and set of units in the game with a select few only being accessable in the campaign. This makes sense in the context of the gameplay since bases can only spawn one type of unit for everyone but it doesn't help the variety of the game. It's not a terrible design overall it just offers little in replaybility and makes the game much simpler and shorter than it could be.
-------------------------
I was torn on recommending this game or not for awhile since it's really not terrible, just not memorable. My final verdict for Oil Rush is NOT recommended. There are much better games out there that do all this game does and more and does it better. For a similar but superior game check out Divinity: Dragon Commander.

It has certainly been a while since i played this game and want to say my PTSD has dropped so i guess i might as well review the game. Oh dear god no. Well i am reviewing the game in a pro / con style and ending the game with my conclusion. I want to warn you that i am review the game in 2016 not based on when it came out. You have been warned.
Pro:
The guns sound pretty cool. I really enjoy the sound of jacob snipers mainly since i played as the sniper dude primarily. Yes i really dont know how to spell his name so i am calling him the sniper dude. Regardless firing the guns felt like a treat with how the guns sound. The guns simply had a charming sound i like.
Each character you choose has their own abilities and unique perks the player could choose from. This helps separate the different play styles that can be obtained with each character such as running in killing everyone with your fists or hanging back and picking people off with your sniper.
The guns leveled up the more you used them, that was pretty cool to see that me killing enemies was worth something more than just exp and money. Now my accuracy with a sniper is even higher or i do more damage with headshot or whatever. It felt that every kill i did ment something more.
Con:
Is there a story? That is a legit question since i honestly do not know. Pretty much the game progression is mission based where you dont necessarily get plot related exposition. When i played through the game it felt that i am just doing missions and not progressing any story what so ever. I want to say you do like five or seven mission till you get to some major plot related part where you get a vault peice and then the game slows back down and that means more missions that feel there for padding. If we take out all the padding i think the game would last for like one and a half hours long.
Wall of text when accepting a mission. I dont know if this is how they explain the story or what not but no one has the time to read something that is more than a few sentences long. It kills the pacing of the game to finish killing a ton of enemies to be greeted by a large ammount of text probably used a exposition..
The wasteland is boring. What killed me more than the feeling of lack of progression is being in the wasteland for about 99% of the game. It is brown really makes me tired. I enjoy seeing more locations rather than strictly wasteland.
Was there music? Well i dont know because i turned it off after my playthrough. None of the music really stood out to me as entertaining or gave me a feeling of a cohesive atmosphere. So yea music is a negative.
Dlc was it great? Well it did add more to the story but struggled being all around interesting. Alot of bosses were just too much for one person soloing who is a sniper character. The zombie island one I will give a like since it has zombies and i certainly do enjoy a good zombie experience. Not that it was great but was something to do, slaughtering undead. Other dlc i can sum up as just meh.
Moxxies underdome....Yea that dlc is just horrible. Your in this survival mode where you kill wave on wave of enemies. Ok but that is not all says the game. You must also survive the buffs or debuffs that the player or enemies experience on every round. Now i roll my eyes in annoyance but that is not all says the game. You must survive 5 rounds made up of 5 waves each round which means a total of 25 waves. Now i slam my head against my desk but that is not all says the game. After doing that for each of the 3 respective arena's you can do it all over again but this time you will have 20 or 25 rounds made up of 5 waves per round. At this point i turn off the game to prevent the game from saying but wait there is more to this dlc. It has not story soooo why is it even here? It isnt even fun, it is a misserable chore to do.
Fires a shot from a powerful gun and get no hit even when i am aiming right at the enemy. Yea there is this nasty little issue where sometimes your bullets dont count. You fire a shot and you know you hit them but the game is like hahaha no you didnt and you just wasted some useful ammo for your most powerful gun.
Fires a shot from a powerful gun and get a damage counter of 0. I am not joking with this. It is similar to the issue just above but this time i get an indication i hit them and the damage i see is 0. I am a higher level than the enemy and using a higher level gun but still manage to get a damage output of 0.
Conclusion:
This game was just too much for me to do. After i got my 100% list i was done and took a break from it. I should of done a review earlier but had PTSD from the game. I can not recommend the game for 2 reasons. 1 all the issues i pointed out in my list. 2 if you get borderlands 2; it has a story and gives a really brief segment about what happened in borderlands 1. So with that you can skip the game entirely and not be confused about the sequal. Again this game probably was good way back then but now it just is not, i recommend borderlands 2 over this because it is in everyway better. Good to see the developers took peieces of this game and made a master peice with it's sequal.

Great hack/slash rouge-like. Very Diablo I or Binding of Isaac. It has a traditional take on isometric bullet-hail, while still reinventing the wheel on combat styles. The BoI-style of relics and potions per cycle make every playthrough a new experience. A constant array of updates and fanservicing bonuses, and more than a few dlc that are reasonably priced. In the five years I've been playing, the game has dramatically improved to the point that I can't recall what the game was beforehand. However, with all the updates it makes long-run characters become obsolete after a certain number of updates. A lot of items can't be scaled with the updates, either, so a classic dilema of Blizzard-esque games' accounts losing value after some time. In higher levels, the bullet-hail proceedurly generated enemies can also flood the screen making it difficult to discern your wepons from an enemy's. The bullets can also bog the game down if you aren't spec'ed for high volume animations on your pc. Depth in the isometric field can be an issue, but with certain "relics" the map becomes entirely explorable. Game runs very well with a controller (I use an xbox-360 controller, but really anything on a usb could work). It plays nomimally on keyboard. The online play has also improved dramatically during the time I've played. It is very similar to the Dibalo III Seasons and cooperative play is very enjoyable when the servers are functioning. High-speed bandwith is recommended for clear gameplay online with the bullet-hails.
Believe me, you'll be left in awe

I am not a fan of the Warriors series, as I always find them lacking in GAMEPLAY department. However, I find that One Piece Pirate Warriors 3 is interesting despite it being the Warriors game, but still, it has its flaws. Here is my opinion:
[ ★★☆☆☆ ]
It is a BIG MEH, due to the fact that the port comes from previous gen, with very little fine-tuning to suit as PC tittle, not the latest gen. However, OPPW3 is not the graphic-intense game, and because of the art style, it doesn't suffer that much, but still looks inferior compared to what it can be.
You can change that with SweetFX / ReShade. It helps to some degree, with some annoying side that you have to disable Steam-Overlay too avoid the intense brightness cause by the overlay popping up. So I have to disable it or either take it offline in order to use other features. There is also an Unlocker to help reducing enemies fading in-out by increasing draw distance, and etc. It's nice to use, with some downside that it may CTD your game after continuous play.
[ ★★★★★ ]
Original JAP voices, I am glad that they don't remove it to put in some cheap ENG dubbed voices.
[ ★★★☆☆ ]
It's warriors game alright. I am not very fond of button-mashing BRAWLER, however, OPPW3 has added in some functions from MELEE make it a little more interesting, Dashing. You can dash-cancel your move to get out of harms, which is a positive imo, instead of waiting for animations to play out, and get hit/knocked back by the enemies attack in the middle.
It also serves as your combo connector, where you can resume your combo after each dash. This make each combat flows better, and faster, but again, still a mindless, button mashing Warriors game in the end.
There are some flaws, but the major one, imo, is the balance. OPPW3 is EXTREMELY easy, heavily lacks of challenging factors. I started playing this on hard difficulty, and haven't toned it down ever since. In other previous Warriors, the hardest difficulty will send you back to tittle screen very fast if you are going to play it this way.
You can 100% each mission easily in one go if it doesn't required you to play as several character to do certain tasks, or certain task that will be unavailable if you finish doing main missions too fast, so that you have to slow down in order to accomplish that task. (have to left most enemies alive to keep blocking the main mission to buy more time, while clearing the minimal route for the side missions to complete just in time) These are the result from no enemy scaling, so when you are buffed enough, you are more or less swoop through the map with little to no resistance.
[ ★★★☆☆ ]
It's one of the better Warriors game for the gameplay, faster, a little less clunky. However, it suffers a lot from the balances. The game is too casual, extremely easy. There is no challenge to complete missions, which make grinding things a not so good experience. This is one of the game that make me use Guides so early in order to reduce mindless grinding without fun.
Apart from that, One Piece fans will love it. Recommended at discounted price.

It's a Koei WARRIORS game people, so if you're not used to them i'll give you a quick rundown because in their template they're pretty much all the same :
* You pick a character between those available and get dumped on a battlefield
* You have a small army and some allies and they have a bigger army full of commanders
* Beat the guys the stage tells you to beat and you win
* Mind the enemy commanders: they're the ones you should be trying to defeat, the foot soldiers are just there to be cannon fodder and add to your bodycount.
* Sometimes the stages have different objectives, like "do X before Y flees" or "escort some random person to a specific spot on the map". Some are easy to do, others like timed missons might be a litte more complicated.
* It's not hard to play, alternate between weak and strong attacks, mow down legions of enemies and feel like a major badass.
* You'll be a one man army regardless of who you pick, but do not expect the same of your AI companions, they'll often fail to solve stuff by themselves and might get in trouble from time to time, getting their butts kicked by commanders or foot soldiers who gang up on them.
*  The same can be said of your foot soldiers who make a huge amount of effort to be almost useless in battle, if some commander or hero unit land in a important base that your army is holding, and there's no companions other than soldiers there, do not leave them unattended.
* Bosses aren't too difficult, just mind their attack patterns and you'll do fine.
* The music is always great: SAMURAI WARRIORS likes techno, DYNASTY WARRIORS is into metal, this game loves rock, metal and jazz and will make you love it too.
* Some battles turn into real slugfests where you can't actually tell what the whazoop is going on: because the objectives change, new people might arrive in the battlefield, another army might come to the party and get into a scuffle with you and the other army you were already fighting with or the lead commander from the  opposing army might withdraw from combat and leave someone else in charge,  they even might go desperate and attempt some stupid strategy. Anything can happen really.
*  After clearing  the story mode once you'll usually have new characters to play and upgrade, and a lot of stupid extra modes to spend time with them.
