I really wasn't expecting much from this game I only have it because a friend gave it to me and I felt obligated to play it, but I'm glad I did because the game is actually a lot of fun.
I don't like the anime, so I really don't think I have any kind of bias supporting it at all. This is probably why I am getting sick of the story mode right now since the cut-scenes can drag on for quite a while and I found myself skipping them a lot when I got the general jist of what the scene was about (sometimes even before that) and I would sometimes lose the context of a curtain fight.
But this IS a fighting game so the story isn't important what is important is the fighting system and I really like it. It's quite unique from other fighting games I've played and still manages to keep a kind of "easy to learn, hard to master" element.
Most of the characters are pretty ballenced, except for the ones that have very fast acting far-ranged moves (like the exploding birds from what-his-face) that make fighting them with another character a real chore when it requires a lot more skill to beat someone who's just spamming the X button all day that is just as strong as special attacks, but doesn't use any energy for some reason.
I wish the game had a few more options though, it's basically a boring story mode, or fight other people online. With the amount of resorces the delveopers put into the story mode I feel like they could have toned it down a little to allow room for other features.
But I digress, the fighting system was enough fun for me to sink more then 10 hours into the game, I just feel like the game could have used at least one other feature instead of another 3 hours of cut-scenes for the story mode.

It takes a lot for me to actually like an MMO enough to actually want to go out there and say, "Hey, world!  Yea, you!  Get this game."  I will start out by saying that if you've ever played and liked Star Wars Galaxies, this game will fill the gaping wound that Sony Online left in your life.  'nuff said, there.  If you liked SWG then get this game.
For everyone that has not played SWG, a bit of a gameplay walkthrough.  The game starts out very well for an alpha MMO, with a fully featured newbie area and tutorials enough to give you a really good foundation of all the skills a new player may want to play with.  You get basic training in several weapon types for free and the ability to spend training credits on up to three others, with the ability to choose from any weapon type the game has to offer. You also get basic crafting tutorials that give you enough of an idea how the surprisingly complex crafting system works to get you on your feet, and gives you a preview of how the really complex things will work once you get that far.  You are also introduced to Entertaining, for providing temporary buffs to allies; Stealth and Rouge-like options, like trap detection and disarming; Animal Taming and Robotic pets; and Medical skills.  And as you play through the tutorial area you get a feel for just how much more there is to play with as you progress with the game.  With dozens of different skills across 6 different catagories.  Even with the comprehensive tutorials, the game is overwhelming at first.  This game has a LOT of mechanics, although they are not so bad that they get in your way.
I definitely recommend it for anyone that's tired of the cookie cutter WoW clones that have been coming out for the last few years.  They definitely stray from the textbook MMO here and it is so refreshing.

This game is the most boring, yet addictive game I've ever played. It's like eating plain potato chips: It doesn't taste very good, and after a short amount of time you begin to feel sick, but it's easier than finding something else to do.
Combat has no variation whatsoever. Every single character shoots in four directions, moves at the same speed, and has the same agonizingly slow stat growth and agonizingly slow, boring gameplay. There is no variation from the easiest difficulty to the hardest, and there can be no strategy involved. The enemies are re-skinned versions of the last thing you fought with more HP and (occasionally) a "skill" that lets them do something other than walk at you slowly for a few seconds.
None of the characters are varied or interesting. If you play as a ranged character, you shoot. If you play as a melee character, you hit things. Again, no difference in movement speed, attack damage or type, or even visual effects aside from a recolor of projectiles.
To top it all off, the game is more focused on selling the player a bunch of DLCs and FTP-style premium currency to buy hats with, but in a paid game. I've played this game for fifty hours trying to make it fun. I bought all of the DLC, visited all of the areas, and ultimately wasted my time and money. There are plenty of good games out there for what this costs, go have a real experience.
EDIT: The mobile version also costs twice as much as the PC version. Go figure.

Enemies scale up a bit faster than you do, and once dead they stay dead, so there's a strange sort of progression going on there since you can't grind forever.
Similar to the first game, the encounter rate is through the roof. Fortunately you can skip a good number of encounters by simply ignoring the monsters. There's far less quests, but most of the quests in the first game were pretty pointless to begin with, so I guess this is can be seen as a good thing.
Fortunately the mini-games are toned down and varied, and luckily opening treasures has no failure. So it's nice to have freebies every now and then to break up the monotony.
The story, as best I can tell, bears no relation to the first game. Not that either one is special, anyhow.
If you like Puzzle Quest 1, I'd say this is a worthy addition. If match-three games aren't your thing, this game won't do anything to appease that feeling. I'll give this an 8.

Hero Siege is a game that wants to be Diablo 2. Sometimes it feels like D2, sometimes it sounds like it, sometimes it plays like it. But it's not D2. There's no real comprehensive story, so if that's what you need in a game, this isn't for you. The voice acting is meh, but that's not what this game is about either. There are also definitely still lots of bugs, so again, if that turns you off, don't buy this.
What's charming about this game is that it doesn't take itself too seriously. You choose a preset class which has a small tech tree which you will fill out before you're done with your first pass through the game. Those classes have range or melee attacks, and then you progressively get skills for your shoulder and trigger buttons. Sure, that's pretty typical. You gather equipment through gameplay, you get skill points to get better... yeah, yeah, yeah. What's FUN about this is the relics. You pick up random♥♥♥♥♥♥that does random♥♥♥♥♥♥for you, both passively and actively. You get one active at a time and one passive at a time. And honestly, by the time you're collecting these, you're probably going to be so BEEFY that you're just choosing what's funniest. There's one that turns all your enemies on the screen into green apples with a silly voice saying "Salummmmm" and another where a creepy stick man runs around giggling saying something dumb and following up with "Heeeheeeh, my balls are sweaty". He hits some things and leaves. One playthrough, I played an amazon with spears bigger than my character and threw them so fast you couldn't tell one spear from the next. THAT is what makes this game charming.
Once you beat the first playthrough/difficulty, you play again on the next level up. Rinse, wash, repeat. The levels are waves of enemies and the bosses sometimes have interesting mechanics. But if you're like me and you want to do every dungeon, explore every crypt, and finish every quest, you will be way overleveled and the cool mechanics will start to feel trite. Sure, you could just jump up a difficulty, but there are different main bosses. You don't get all the achievements if you skip levels. So realistically, it's probably run up its fun for me.
Also keep in mind it's HEAVILY bugged. If you play with other people you're in for a ride. Puzzles don't sync up so you have to do them separately... most of the time. Sometimes you can help each other. Sometimes lag will kill one or the whole team. And the hit box for leaving areas is atrocious. Seriously, I lost a ton of loot because one of us was trying to get our♥♥♥♥♥♥and hit the ladder out of a place. The worst.
But... I'm impressed. This very tiny dev team is still working on this. They're raising money by offering you skins and content to cover server and update costs. And honestly, I think that's cool. Yeah it's more money. But what it's adding isn't necessary. You're essentially saying "Thanks, dev team. Have some money so you can keep doing what you're doing." And I think that transparency is what makes me like them more than any of this. I think some day this game is going to be an absolute gem. For now.. it's a pretty fun game.
Also, keep in mind, this game can be played local co-op (where most of my hours went to before I bought the game myself) but it is WAY WAY WAY better played over the internet. That said, sync problems. Two evils. Pick one.

Puzzle Quest is a cross between a JRPG and Bejeweled, with a minigame similar to the latter acting as a proxy for combat. As in Bejeweled, spaces on the board are cleared by forming rows of matching colors, and empty areas are filled with additional tiles that drop in from offscreen. If you're lucky, the gems that drop in will match adjacent gems and cause additional cascades of damage to your enemy; many people have observed that this "luck" seems to happen much more frequently in the computer-controlled opponent's favor than it does the player's.

Scientists have demonstrated that many primates have an innate sense of fairness: if you give one monkey a greater reward than another received for the same task, they notice and become hostile. That being said, it's a given that nearly all artificial intelligence in video games cheats to some degree, since this is the easiest, most reliable way that a computer can present any sort of challenge to the human brain. Because of this sensitivity to unfairness we share with other primates, though, an important part of video game AI is not that it avoid cheating--which is extraordinarily difficult--but that it avoid the APPEARANCE of cheating. A single glimpse of obvious cheating by the computer is often enough to completely ruin a game forever.

Puzzle Quest's developers claim that the game doesn't cheat, and more specifically that it doesn't know the makeup of the gems that will fall into the board after a move; I'm not convinced. What I am sure of, though, is that it FEELS like the computer is cheating, and it made the time I spent playing this game one of the most frustrating and least rewarding experiences of my life.

A good story, with a nod to old tech interfaces (DOS), along with a slight detective feel and anime-styled art. There are cute anime chicks involved, as well as the ability to choose chat options with them in between reading.
In this story, you are a solo space traveler on an apparent contract job. (No you don't get to fly the ship.) Your job is to find out what happened to an old asian colony ship. With the help of the old ships AI(s), you have to dig up as much information on what happened to the crew through reading logs and eventually download the information for your client. While reading logs, the AI will ask you about what you read, or make a statement about the character(s) or problems involved with the entry, allowing you to get a bit more insight as to what happened. This gives a unique environment where you feel as if you are reading along side an AI, and can at times really get into the story.
It does not take long to get through the game, but expect a ton of reading. Purely a virtual novel at heart, but with a 'choose your own story' ending, thus creating a much more interactive environment than other VNs like the Sakura Paradise game (Where you really have no control over the game besides watch and hit next).
This story has a very large dose of maltreatment of the sexes... specificly the fairer sex, and points towards cultures that used to, and still do, treat them very poorly. The game is rather obvious fairly quickly in showing their agenda to create a sense of oppression which may be quite real in the world, may still be unwelcome to some players. So you have been warned if that is of little or no interest to you.
After the game is done, there is little replay value besides getting the achievements, all the endings, and/or all the entries, yet the game does give you a feeling of completion and does not leave you 'in the dark' about anything, aside for what happens to your character and the AI after the game ends... but that is what the sequel is for.
Hope this review helped some of you make a decision on this game~

Estranged: Act I
-----------------
When I first downloaded this game, I was skeptical. Firstly, it was free: sure, they probably couldn't make it paid because it's a blatant HL2 Mod, but all legal aspects aside great quality shouldn't be expected in a free game. Secondly, I'd seen some of the reviews on the Estranged community page: "This mod sucks!" "No quality!" "I like cheese!". But what the hell, when did I listen to random people over the Internet? So I tried the game.
Turns out, whoa, it isn't half bad. Spanning about an hour and a half, one can take comfort in the fact that future installments will give you an overall decent playtime. The environments are quite beautiful in places: an observant player might notice some props and textures from HL2, but there's plenty of custom materials in this game to give it a fairly unique feel. There's also a good soundtrack, which at one point made me super pumped and ready to kick some♥♥♥♥♥
There's two kinds of enemy in this first act: firstly, dumb running zombies. They look more like hobos on some kind of drug, which is cool, because killing frenzied druggies is way better than killing headcrab zombies. They can even play dead sometimes, which gave me a jumpscare on two separate occasions. The second type of enemy is, more disappointingly, a HL2 rebel. Of course, this time they're hostile and flashlight-wielding, and actually quite a challenge to take down if you aren't well-equipped. Thankfully, these elite hostiles don't come into play until quite near the end.
There's a fair few action sequences where you're gunning down whatever stands in your path, but also a lot of platforming and puzzle parts. The kind of structure that made HL2 a great game, I suppose. Running around in super tense situations before cooling down with a bit of crate-stacking and vent-crawling. There was never a moment when I wanted to quit because I got bored, and the shots just kept on coming.
Overall, good game. Buy it. It's free, which is the best price ever. So no excuses.

This is one of those rare instances where an early access game gets abandoned, and then the developers come back to it. In fact, if I'm not mistaken, this is the only such instance. So I am changing my "Do not Recommend" to "Recommended".
What makes this game any different than any others? Depth. There is so much depth to this game, that it would be impossible to learn it all in even a month. There are thousands of recipes, billions of combinations of what you can do. A deep crafting system and a cool sci-fi world to play in.
The game still needs some work, but after being gone for almost a year or more, I suspect not much was done during that time. They always promised it would come back, but if you've played early access before, you've heard that line before. I am impressed with these developers that they actually made good on their promise.
I've heard this compared to Star Wars Galaxies, and I think that is a fair comparison. I would maybe throw Ultima Online in there as well. There is so much to do that it would be impossible for you to do it all yourself, which forces you to actually be social and play with other people.
I was very disappointed when the game went down, and when I was told today it was back I was very excited to play. Unfortunately, as of right now, the game is EXTREMELY laggy. I have faith they will fix this issue. Their initial reason for shutting down was because of some kind of legal rights with the engine, again, I thought it was a lie. But seeing them coming back, even though they had already made a ton of money, shows integrity. The developers are very helpful and friendly as well when you contact them in game.
So if you're looking for a highly complex sci-fi MMORPG, this is what you've been looking for.Just be warned, this game has a STEEP learning curve. Perhaps the steepest learning curve of any game I've played besides EVE. I think Repop is better, but that's opinion.
Ultimately, it's up to you if you decide to get it, but this is not the game you just hop in and play casually. You can play casually, but you're going to forget stuff because there is so much to do.
If you get it, I think you will enjoy it. And you always have 2 hours (or 2 weeks, whichever comes first) to get a refund, so you literally have nothing to lose by trying it.

I have 4 hours invested in the game so far (a little more actually) so my opinion will change, I'm sure. For now, I can sum my opinion up as "disappointed".
It's not an outright failure, but it's not a raving success either.
My problem with it is that I'm an adult, with adult responsibilities and duties in real life. There's something to be said for the "tried and true" algorithm  when it comes to MMO gaming - everyone is at least partially familiar with it, it doesn't take a novel-length read to comprehend the basic essentials of game play and people can mostly jump right in and start playing... even if they don't have all the finer details down.
The Repopulation defies this, but in doing so, I feel will end up alienating a lot of potential players.
The phrase "easy to learn, difficult to master" doesn't apply here. The game is difficult to learn and somewhat impossible to master.
The tutorials are about as clear as mud, not because they're poorly written but because they have to explain every detail to you before you can even start to understand what the basic functions of the game are. The skills are some type of hybrid between the old UO system and their own specialized system of learning. You'll spend your first few hours totally lost, wondering why you can't do 90% of the things you thought you'd be able to, only to find there's some convoluted method to learning a simple skill.
Things are just complicated for the sake of being complicated it seems. Item quality is another one here, as are skill levels. Different levels with other numbers, with an alphabetical listing or something or other... Christ! Just trying to figure out what almost every other MMO has made an essential part of their game brings on a rage-induce migraine in this game!
Combine this with working a job, having a family and bills to pay.... you see where that disappointment comes from now?
This isn't just a game I can sit down and enjoy, and feel like I accomplished something... anything... in a couple of hours worth of play.
There are other issues that I could almost overlook if the core of the game was at lest enjoyable, which it is currently not:
- Your character is a clone, so they got this right. Everyone looks like a clone of one another though. Armor is determined at the start and very little about it actually changes throughout the game. After 4 hours, I find myself getting tired and bored of looking exactly the same as I did when I first spawned into he game. other players also look the same... everyone looks the same.
You can customize your features, but that does little when you immediately cover them up with a full suite of armor.
- Whatever the hell determines heavy from medium, from light, is a total mystery. There are no indicators when you choose your armor and since you choose it before you see any skills, you really have nothing to go on when you initially start the game.
It also never changes. You get upgrades for it, but the actual armor never changes for anything different.
Call me shallow, but the best idea of a graphical MMO (I played MUDs before this) is that you can see a graphical image of your character. You can mix and match things to look unique or have special functions that others can see... show off almost.
So when you see the "let's play" videos and screenshots of everyone playing the same characters,... yeah, that's really how it looks.
- Maybe because it's an alien planet? The gravity feels like a fraction of what it should be. You can jump off a ledge, straight, push a direction mid-air and change directions. Jumping feels slow and awkward. Animations in general seem slower than the actions should take.
All of those things might be "Alpha" issues but they add up.
- The concept isn't bad, but the only ting I've seen so far is its influence on NPC activity. Some go to bed for night, others come out to work, and so on.
This cycle only exaggerates another issue that relates to it and that is the questing. You don't have to complete quests, but it sure helps if you do. Unfortunately when you take a quest and find the guy you need to talk to went to sleep for the night, it puts a damper on your plans to actually finish the quest in any reasonable time frame.
Questing is already bad enough. Add to it, the headache of trying to time it with the day-night cycle and it's a completely unneeded, overly exaggerated pain in the♥♥♥♥♥

tl;dr I give this game a 6/10. If you are a huge fan of naruto be sure to pick it up, but if you're not you might want to buy something else instead.
First let's talk about the story and animation of the game. I really enjoyed the animation sequences and story mode, because it was like watching the anime but in cell-shaded 3D graphics. I have never watched the episodes that this game was based off of, and it made it that much more enjoyable because it caught me up to speed. That being said, the plot was a little too predictable for me and boring at times.
The gameplay of this game is OK. It feels kind of like a generic action game, but it has a chakra system and combo system which adds some depth. The kunai throwing does not seem to have any use. The time it takes to throw the kunai is time you could be using to close the gap on the opponent, and the damage the kunai does is so little that it's not even worth it. There are some issues with the combo system though, mainly that there is always going to be one combo that does the most damage and is usable in every situation. To avoid this they should have made multiple top-damage combos that are each used in different situations.
The UI and title screen could use some work, and I also had some issues getting the game to run at a proper frame rate. It had nothing to do with my hardware, but with the default settings that the game had. I would say that even though the game is good, the port of the game was very sloppy.
I give this game a 6/10. It is an above average game, but does not score higher than a 6 because of its bland combo system and port issues.

ClickRaid is possibly the most unique clicker/idle game out there, simply because it features online multiplayer. Up to five people can join a server and support each other as they progress through the game. If you don't have an internet connection for whatever reason, single player offline play is also an option. Aside from clicker staples like rebirths and heroes, this game also has quests, leaderboards, and guilds. Guilds are groups of friends that have their own separate chat, and are noted by three letters. This game is updated frequently and has seasonal events that can boost your progress. There's also a class system that can give you specific upgrades to your team. Overall, this is easily one of the best games in the genre, and I would recommend it to any clickaholic.

The Repopulation... Where to start?
This game I heared about before it went into a playable Alpha state. And, it intrigued me. It's an MMOSBRPG, or Massively Multiplayer Online Sandbox Role Playing Game (Long Abbreviations FTW!). And, here's my review of this.
Graphics: Current: 7.5/10 Future: ?/10: So, since this game is an alpha, I have to review what is given to me. And, it's pretty good, but I can't push the high quality, due to my machine not quite being able to play at max with a good framerate, though with the upgrades that I want to purchase, maybe then i'll be able to play at 144 FPS on Ultra for this game. The game looks nice, but the character animations are a bit lazy, but they will change with time. Oh, and Dual Wielding Pistols is really funky... You hold both pistols in the same physical location, leading to some funny clipping stuff.
Overall Gameplay: 9/10
Combat: 10/10: This game has such a unique combat system. It has one main governing system, the Openings System. If you shoot someone in the Leg, they are the suceptible to other things like maybe Bleeding, or if someone is Startled because of how close you got to them from a shot or slash, then maybe you can Dishearten them and make them deal less damage. Any way you slice it, this game does not have "Basic" attacks, each and every attack has some flavor of modifier. And that is really cool!
Crafting: 7.5/10: Ok, this is the meat and potatoes of this game. I can't go over each aspect of crafting in this review, because it would be a 20 page college level paper... If you want the details, The Repopulation Forums are a great place to go to learn about crafting! Basically, you gather materieals, such as Contaminated Water, Hides, Wood, Berries, Metal Ores, etc. and process them into components to make other things, such as Fittings which will have their own spotlight in the next section. The main problem with the crafting is, there is soo much crafting that you will probably make your head explode trying to do it all, but fear not, you can still make money as a gatherer through the Work Orders system which will be talked about in it's own section.
Gear System: 10/10: This game has a fantastic gear system that revolves around 100% Customization. Every Gear Item is a shell, you put Fittings into the shells to give them buffs such as Physical Resistance or Penetration, or Burning status effects, or more Health, or more Endurance, or more Momentum Retention, just about every stat in the game is given through Fittings you put in your Armor or Weapons.
Auction House: 10/10: This is one of the best parts about the game, the "Auction House" It has several functionalities such as Work Orders and a plain auction house ripped straight from WoW. Work Orders allow gatherers and crafters to work together to get items in exchange for Credits (this game's currency) a Crafter can put out a Work Order from anywhere in the world (you can also buy and put things on the Auction House anywhere in the world) and a Gatherer or other Crafter can put in the items to fufill the Work Order and get a posted amount of Credits for their assistance.
Final Verdict: 8.5/10: The game needs some polish definately, but this F2P MMOSBRPG I believe will become a titan in the industry that dominates over WoW and ESO, and SW:ToR. You can buy into the Alpha with the Silver and Gold Packages right here on Steam and get some extra benefits when the game goes live some time in Q4 of this year! But the game will be 100% Free To Play, with the cash shop being 100% Cosmetic Items Only.

First Impressions:
Let me just start off by saying I'm definitely one of those 90s kids who grew up with Toonami and all that, so the nostalgia factor has been pretty intense from the moment I started the game up with Cha La Head blasting.  I'm not a DBZ fan in particular, but I did enjoy it.  I picked this up during the sale because I don't mind grindy, MMO-esque games, as long as they're vibrant and fun to play.  So far I'm not disappointed, but I can imagine if you're a fan of the hardcore DBZ fighting games that this might not be up your alley, since combat feels fairly simple once you take your lumps in the first few missions.
The most appealing aspect was being able to make my own character in the DBZ universe, and there's a decent amount of options for the races they offer.  You can change armor and even armor color later pretty effortlessly, too.  They're all presets however, no sliders here, so that may be an issue for some.  Your race matters too, and some characters will take note of just who you chose to be.
The world hub has some convenience flaws, like not being able to dash to get to where you're going faster.  You're given some decent preset motions and texts to interact with others, which helps bring your character alive a bit more outside the story's cutscenes.  It's a bit confusing at first as nothing is unlocked and you're vaguely told to go talk to everyone.
Controller support is good, but I'm using a DS4 and the game insists on thinking I have a numbered gamepad instead of showing the buttons for a 360 controller, which is easier to translate in my head.  Once you learn what's what it's fine, but makes learning a bit difficult if you're a player who's going to be using a Dualshock.
Running on a 970 on Windows 10, no framerate issues at all or tearing after I turned v-sync on.  Everything looks crisp, bright, and shiny.  Music's good quality and clear, voices are.. fairly what I'd expect, for better or worse haha.
So far, it's definitely a recommend if you're coming in expecting a fan experience, but not some groundbreaking, amazing game.
Updated impressions @ Lv. 50:
Definitely leaning more toward recommending only if one is a DBZ fan.  The atmosphere and experience do make up for a lot of the flaws and some odd design choices, like slipping in super hard Parallel Quests in the lower tiers where it seems like the enemies never stop coming.  Frustrating stuff.  Combat gets a lot smoother as you power up and learn, but the game really does not hold your hand at all through the process of learning about armor, stats, and builds so you can succeed.  Being able to preview gear before you buy it would have been a welcome feature as well.
Took me about 14 hours to get through the story with some Parallel Quest grinding.  Lots more replayability than just those hours of course, as there are still characters and places I have yet to encounter.

What a suprisingly great game! You play as a spy (think Inspector Gadget) who's missions consist of stealing video tapes, taking out targets, or simpy hacking into  corporate servers to get info that you in turn can use to help the Corporation or bring it down. This game also gives you decisions story-wise that allow you to be the morally "good" guy or if it's your thing you can be a murderous "bad" guy. The story is not long by any means, you should be able to finish it in about 2-3 hours. The replayability is definitely there though. Each mission gets graded which makes you want to go back and beat your old score. You can beat the game in a few different ways. It's also backed with steam workshop, so you can create your own missions and confrontations or just play someone other persons creation.
Gameplay wise think "Mark of the Ninja" mixed with "Watch Dogs". The mechanics are heavy on stealth and strategy. There is no one way to complete a mission, instead the game gives you options on how you want to beat each level. Want to kill everyone and leave no witnesses? You can. Want to sneak past every gaurd after you hack the lights and beat the mission without killing anyone? You can. Want to just knock their asses unconscious and move freely? You can. In between each mission is a shop where you can purchase items (Revolver, etc..) and spend upgrade points (Higher jump, faster jump charge time, etc..) I would recommend this game to anyone who likes strategy, nior mysteries, or dudes in trench coats.

Hero Siege is a game that wants to be Diablo 2. Sometimes it feels like D2, sometimes it sounds like it, sometimes it plays like it. But it's not D2. There's no real comprehensive story, so if that's what you need in a game, this isn't for you. The voice acting is meh, but that's not what this game is about either. There are also definitely still lots of bugs, so again, if that turns you off, don't buy this.
What's charming about this game is that it doesn't take itself too seriously. You choose a preset class which has a small tech tree which you will fill out before you're done with your first pass through the game. Those classes have range or melee attacks, and then you progressively get skills for your shoulder and trigger buttons. Sure, that's pretty typical. You gather equipment through gameplay, you get skill points to get better... yeah, yeah, yeah. What's FUN about this is the relics. You pick up random♥♥♥♥♥♥that does random♥♥♥♥♥♥for you, both passively and actively. You get one active at a time and one passive at a time. And honestly, by the time you're collecting these, you're probably going to be so BEEFY that you're just choosing what's funniest. There's one that turns all your enemies on the screen into green apples with a silly voice saying "Salummmmm" and another where a creepy stick man runs around giggling saying something dumb and following up with "Heeeheeeh, my balls are sweaty". He hits some things and leaves. One playthrough, I played an amazon with spears bigger than my character and threw them so fast you couldn't tell one spear from the next. THAT is what makes this game charming.
Once you beat the first playthrough/difficulty, you play again on the next level up. Rinse, wash, repeat. The levels are waves of enemies and the bosses sometimes have interesting mechanics. But if you're like me and you want to do every dungeon, explore every crypt, and finish every quest, you will be way overleveled and the cool mechanics will start to feel trite. Sure, you could just jump up a difficulty, but there are different main bosses. You don't get all the achievements if you skip levels. So realistically, it's probably run up its fun for me.
Also keep in mind it's HEAVILY bugged. If you play with other people you're in for a ride. Puzzles don't sync up so you have to do them separately... most of the time. Sometimes you can help each other. Sometimes lag will kill one or the whole team. And the hit box for leaving areas is atrocious. Seriously, I lost a ton of loot because one of us was trying to get our♥♥♥♥♥♥and hit the ladder out of a place. The worst.
But... I'm impressed. This very tiny dev team is still working on this. They're raising money by offering you skins and content to cover server and update costs. And honestly, I think that's cool. Yeah it's more money. But what it's adding isn't necessary. You're essentially saying "Thanks, dev team. Have some money so you can keep doing what you're doing." And I think that transparency is what makes me like them more than any of this. I think some day this game is going to be an absolute gem. For now.. it's a pretty fun game.
Also, keep in mind, this game can be played local co-op (where most of my hours went to before I bought the game myself) but it is WAY WAY WAY better played over the internet. That said, sync problems. Two evils. Pick one.

So, if you like what you see, buy it. It'll only get better from there, and it has a dedicated community. If you're holding off because it's in Early Access, at least keep an eye on it.

This piece of ancient entertainment is a bug riddled mess, not just in game, but from the startup menu in general.
When I tried to start it up for the first time in months, I noticed 1 thing when the launcher pulled up. I clicked the client prompt to go through... and it wouldn't launch.

I eventually found out the issue of it. The game can be seen as malware by the anti-virus. The only way for me to play it was 2 ways.
1 - I disable my anti-virus and start it up
2 - I add the client to the exception list of the anti-virus and then relaunch the game.
That sounds like a simple fix. But here's the other issue with it.
Hackershield is utter garbage...
--------------------------
Yeah the little security file that protects your account from being hijacked or... honestly I got no clue what it does. But when I added the client file to the exception list, it ended up disabling the hacker shield.exe file to load properly.
So I load into the game, and not 5 seconds into the game, BAM! I get my account suspended for a few days. Why? Because I hacked past the shield, apparently.
And that's the other issue with the game, the hacker shield thing is utter garbage. I've looked into forum after forum about the damn thing, and there's been reports where people can even get past it and even get past the patch launcher!

Mycaruba:

A Cleaver, and Valencia's Cross Line Plate Armor, both given blessed stats and full durability.

For those of you who have played Digital, you already have some idea of what you're getting yourself into. For those who haven't, be prepared for a beautifully-written, heart-wrenching tale that subtly draws you in via its interface, pacing, and characters. Also, go play Digital. Analogue is, on the surface, a story of a person sent to investigate a derelict spaceship. But that's not right. It's a story of two AIs, the only remaining residents of the ship. But that's not right, either. It's a story of history, of cultural differences, of secrets and questions and unexpected answers. Most of the game is reading, and it can be daunting at first. The initial selection of documents you're given are, admittedly, the least interesting. But stick with it, and you shall be rewarded for your perseverance. Although there are five endings, the nature of the game makes replayability rather low - but it might be worth skimming past the early parts again in order to unlock different documents later on and get a different angle on the story. There are only two real puzzles in the game, and both involve a command prompt interface which I found to be quite fun to use - especially in the delicious second puzzle, much later in the game. If you're not good with computers and reasoning, you might not do so well with that one, but give it a shot anyways. One speed bump is a small price to pay for an overall enriching experience.

-WARNING SPOILERS IN THIS REVIEW, READ AT YOUR OWN DESCRETION-
So, for starters this review is long over due.
But, I still feel obligated to make a review of this game. For the reason that there is obviously going to be a sequel in the near future.
So to kick things off, 'Borderlands', the tag itself is suppose to represent the 'Mad Max' in space FPS experience. But that is not at all what you'd expect in this game, granted 'TellTaleGames' haves never done that, since they do Third-person decision based stories. Which is what I love from this company, but they seemed to almost perfectly get around that by having what we'd expect in 'Tales From the Borderlands', although it's not an FPS, it still contains more then enough action, with an enemy at hand around every corner and different location. Now obviously this all takes place after 'Borderlands 2' which is the last game of its title, with the exception of 'Tales From the Borderlands' where our infamous Anti-Hero, Handsome Jack has died after vault hunters fought him. So the way 'TellTaleGames' decided to keep Jack relevant was they had posters all around the planet Pandora, but that wasn't enough. They made an A.I. (Artificial Intellegence) version of Jack, that only one of the two main characters could see (Rhys). I enjoyed this very much and was very surprised to see the Anti-Hero of the whole universe come back in such an unexpected fashion. But of course there are negatives about everything in life. So I'm just going to go through them a little quickly. Okay for starters, and this goes for all 'TellTaleGames' mind you: The decisions you make, some of them do not tailor to how you play, and don't carry over to the next episode, which kind of defeats the purpose. Another thing is at the end of the game, when you chose the special character, you can only get ClapTrap even though it's a great surprise to see ClapTrap and have his wit be carried through the entire last half of Episode 5. One other thing is when Sasha 'dies', now I put quotes on it because she dies but then cheats death with her adoptive dad's (Felix) gift, now I'm glad they didn't lose someone they loved, but it would've opened up to so much more story and plot development, and a potential climax. But they shut that down. Now, even though this game has some more flaws, they're not as major. But overall this game is good, I recommend it.
I give it a solid 7.5/10

Did you enjoy Star Wars Galaxies, Shadowbane, Anarchy Online, Everquest or Dark Age of Camelot back in the day? Did you enjoy the era where MMO's had more complexity to them? Well, chances are you will enjoy this title. It has everything that made old school MMO's great but with a modern touch.
The problem with MMO's nowadays is that they all follow the same formula: quest, level up, get gear and loot. While this is an OK formula, I missed the more open-ended MMO's where you could go out and do what you wanted without having to follow a linear progressional path. The Repopulation does this right. Similar to SWG (Star Wars Galaxies), the developers made the game so that you could start off and get right into crafting without having to force yourself to do combat. You could do quests if you want, but you can also head right out and follow your destiny.
Want to be a tradesman who earns an honest living building vehicles and houses? You can do that. Want to be one of hundreds of soldiers fighting a war on the battlefield? You can do that. Thing is with this game; there are so many features to it that it really feels like a living, breathing world. Although still in 'Early Access' it feels like a polished Alpha. Granted, there are still MANY bugs and quirks that need fixing. The game would not be acceptable to the average gamer. However, if you have that itch for an old-school MMO like I did, then pick this up. It'll scratch that itch.
I can't speak for the future of this game, but there is a LOT of potential here. The world is quite large as-is and I have a feeling they're planning to expand it. What makes this game feel like an actual world is the complexity of it. It could well be a life simulator once it's released. Only time will tell.
Based on what I've experienced so far and the promise this game shows, I have no choice but to rate it a solid 8/10. However, if they fix the bugs, clunky UI & map glitches and add a little more pizazz to the game, I'd give it a 10/10. This is THE MMO to play for any MMO gamer.

So this is a first person puzzle game much in the same vein as Portal. One of the creators of Portal is also behind this game so there are some similarities. But where Portal was ingenious and funny, Quantum Conundrum is not. The main difference as I see it between the games is that in Portal working out the solution to the puzzle can be a bit hard but once you do the execution of said solution is fairly easy. In Quantum Conundrum it is the exact opposite. The solutions are easy to figure out but the executions can be complex and frustrating. Needless to say, I prefer the Portal-way of doing puzzles.
In Quantum Conundrum you often have to time several jumps on the row which can make it frustrating when you  miss the last jump and have to start over again. On the upside, the checkpoint-system is very generous so you dont have to redo a puzzle from the beginning but you usually continue at exactley the platform-puzzle where you failed.
I found the game easy and it took me about 3 - 4 hours to complete it. The problem is that it seems that they have opted for Quantity instead of Quality when it comes to the puzzle. If you play the game for an extended period of time (over 30 minutes) you get a bit bored by the fact that every puzzle bare some resembles to the one before it which makes it feel that you are essentially solving variations of the same puzzle multiple times. It works to play it in short spurts but over 30 minutes of gametime isn't recommended.
At this point it costs about €9 and I would recommend it when it drops down to $5 and if you have a real craving for a first person puzzle-game. If you haven't played Portal 1 and 2 I would recommend you to do that instead.
Edit: Also, I didn't find the game funny...at all. The portal games are laugh out loud funny to me but this game fell completely flat. I found the narration to be more annoying than anything else.

So far I've played the game for 12 hours, and so far it's everything I've been looking for from an MMO the last 5 years. YES the game is in alpha, but the content that is ALREADY in the game far surpases most mainstream MMO's on the market. Just looking through a list of the mechanics, it warms my gamer heart: for those searching for a 'hardcore' experience, this is where it's at.
Each skill in the game is leveled through use, and as you use the skills and they increase, you open up the amount of skills you get on your action bar. Personally, this skill aquisition system is excellent. Not only are the skills not handed to you (you either have to purchase them with training points or receive as mission rewards) but the way you mold your character is completely up to you. This makes the combat highly customizable, allowing weapon swapping and combining skills and status affects.
As far as the current state of the game, it is very much in alpha, and feels like it. The game is stable enough to play, but some of the features are not in the game (some skills, some missions, etc.) and there is a general clunkiness to everything. This game has me very excited for its future, the crafting is very in depth, the combat is fully customizable and can be switched between action and traditional rpg, and the overall feel of the game is unique and fresh but also nostalgic and genuine.

This is a good game which suffers from being a weak port.
Before I talk about what I liked about this game, here are some issues I had with it...
- The game crashes for me on every other exit.
- The loading screens are annoyingly long. This was especially annoying while trying to 100% the challenge missions.
- Not enough graphic options.
- The game seems to use more resources when running on window mode. I had no framerate issues while running the game on fullscreen.
- Cutscenes. Too many damned cutscenes! The original cutscenes animated for the game were good but a good chunk of it is reused from the anime. It actually feels like the cutscenes were longer than the campaign itself.
Despite all that, the game left a good impression on me.
- The battle system is simple and easy to learn. The set of battle tips found in the start menu did a good job of explaining various mechanics. I think that a proper tutorial such as a practice fight would have been a lot better though.
- The game cutscenes (not the reused anime cutscenes) were done really well.
- The challenge missions were a good challenge. Some of them ranged from really easy to moderately hard.
- Large cast of playable characters. I wish it were larger though.
- Flashy moves!
The game was decent. It has problems that are common among ports but the production quality redeems it to a certain extent.

Pros:
Developer loves his game, he is easy to contact and accepts all suggestions as well as constantly updates this game to improve the play experience. (When its not too hard for him to program)
There is quite a lot of progression included.  At certain stages you unlock a new menu that allows you to expand your experience.
Multiplayer is a huge aspect of this game.  Joining as well as creating and finding people that pick different classes than you do to achieve all available buffs is an important part of this game.  You can play with your friends and that aspect is quite fun.
This game in the past month has evolved to a huge extent.  Today it is 100 times better than it was a month ago and the game seems to keep evolving at that rate.
Cons:
There is little to no afk progression which means that you have to constantly play to get anywhere which really limits the kind of players this game attracts.  The game offers little to nothing to click on or do while you play so a lot of it is just looking at your screen falling asleep pressing prestige button and entering a capcha.  This game causes a lot of segregation so its extremely hard to find players near your skill level to play with often times you will see games with 7k plus stage required and so on making it difficult to join or find rooms.  You end up doing the exact same thing over and over and over for hours on end while not being able to afk which makes a lot of the game design tiring.
This game gets super expensive. The extra support pack doesnt really seem to give you much for the price.  When you buy the game you really dont buy everything a lot of it is DLC expansions so you kind of feel robbed at some point needing to spend $5 on a pet that picks things up and gives you an advantage while not being albe to unlock it is super expensive.
The amount of AFK players is constantly growing even though being afk doesnt do anything for you chances are you as an active player will find a game with 3 or 4 other people and join it only to find that 2 or 3 of the other players have been afk for 20 minutes and you are the reason they are able to stay afk because your farming them raid souls.  Creating your own game hoping to get a group of active players is a task thats almost impossible.  When you create a game it creates as a 1/5 room but anyone that creates a game where players can't join also create 1/5 rooms and no one joines 1/5 rooms because they know that there is a good chance they will get auto kicked because they can't connect to the host so if you want an active game create your own but i myself created a game for 2 hours and had 0 people even attempt to join.  So your choices are play alone or support an afk player and feed them raid souls.
(Some sort of AFK progression even if its at a slower rate than an active player would fix 100% of these issues.)
All the cons aside this game is worth its price tag and it should be tried.

With each new game, the developers (Totem Games) were approaching the time of the steel steam navy and the epic sea battles of the Sino-Japanese War of 1895, the Spanish-American War of 1898 and the Russo-Japanese War of 1905. In this case, the events unfold during the Spanish-American war in the Pacific. Because in reality, the resistance of the Spaniards to the US Asian Squadron (commander George Dewey) was small, the developers had to delve into the history books and to call for help alternative history. In reality, the expedition of the Spanish admiral Manuel de la Cámara to the Philippines was canceled, but the Spanish fleet still had warships that send them to Asia. Thus, we can say that the historical part is on the verge between truth and fiction. Damn, but who cares?
What's new in the game itself? All units and buildings in the game now need to be supplied. Previously, everything was simple - take the biggest and strongest ships and destroy all. Now it is worthwhile to think several times how much the elementary movement of a large warship on the supply route will cost. Captured the enemy harbor and placed there a garrison of infantry - be prepared to spend on its maintenance!  It's cheaper to defend than to attack. All this made the game in a strategic mode more interesting.
What can I say about the simulator mode of combat between ships? At first glance, everything is as before. But if you look closely, it turns out that a very useful function has been added. Now you can visually determine the dangerous distance. Instead of the good old wooden sloops of Lincoln's time, we operate well-armed steel steamships (mostly). From such enemies it is useful to stay away and hope that your shells will fall more often and cause more damage to the enemy. I really do not advise you to engage in close combat, before the enemy ships are badly damaged.
As before, I refrain from recommending this game to everyone. That would be untrue. This is a very special and largely unpolished game, but I like to play it.

A decent indie game that, for the most part, provides excellent co-op and single player game play with a little extra multiplayer on the side that is also a great time-waster. I do recommend it only because I'd like to see this game grow & expand. Unfortunately, it's an early access game. However, despite the extremely slow development this game has been getting, it's on a steady course to becoming a complete game somewhere down the road. I already enjoy this game as is, and imagining it in it's complete stage years from now as a tactical shooter in a realistic sci-fi future excites me.
The community is fairly small and unless you've got a few friends to play with you're likely going to spend most of your time here in early access fooling around in single player fighting robots in a supposed "training simulation" as candidates for the Interstellar Marine program as we await the story to develop. There are two campaign missions plus two maps that host a terrorist hunt style mode, an escape mode, and a gauntlet mode of sorts. The multiplayer is what you would expect in a tactical FPS. There are some frame rate issues I've noticed.
All in all, if you got some money to spend and are looking to waste some time alone or with freinds, I'd definately recommend checking this out.

Wow.... just wow. This game is a must buy!
Let me start out by saying that I've never played a Borderlands game before this one. If you are new to the Borderlands universe, no worries. Tales From The Borderlands is able to introduce you to the world without needing any prior knowledge of the original games. Technically this game takes place after Borderlands 2, but it is summarized perfectly and requires no further knowledge then what they explain to you.
In TFTB, you play two different characters (Rhys and Fiona) as they recap the story of their adventure. Like most other Telltale games, Tales plays out like an interactive adventure, with dialogue options and choices sprinkled in.
The best and most important thing about this game are the characters. In most Telltale games, I only attach to a couple characters and the rest don't really grab me in any way. This was not the case for TFTB. Each character has their own unusual and unique personality. You pick up more and more characters along the way, and each are just as interesting as the last. A lot of credit goes to the voice actors for helping create a fitting personality for each character. You have voices from video game legends; Nolan North and Troy Baker. Along with more big names such as: Patrick Warburton, Erin Yvette and Chris Hardwick. Each actor makes the character their own, and it helps the game tremendously.
Another great thing about TFTB, is the humor. What can I say, it's just hilarious. I found myself laughing out loud several times, which is not something I normally do. There is plenty of goofy and awkward humor, with a lot of sarcasm thrown in there. Some jokes hit and some jokes miss, but it's all so much fun that even when a joke isn't that funny, I was still able to smile and appreciate that it was in there.
TFTB also greatly improved on  the choice mechanics. In many Telltale games such as TWD or TWAU, the choices feel restricted. It usually puts something important in front of you and says "pick this decision or pick that one." There is nothing wrong with that, but TFTB changes that and adds refreshing new elements to the table.
Sure, they still have that "one or the other" scenario here and again, but it doesn't feel so serious and forced.  The new choice options along with the fact that it never takes itself too seriously, is a perfect combination for this game.
Tales From The Borderlands is an action packed, funny, and exciting journey filled with twists and turns. If you are a fan of the series, you'll love the cameos and easter eggs hidden throughout the game. If you are like me, and you've never touched a Borderlands game, it's still a very enjoyable experience that never becomes to difficult to understand.
I would easily give Tales From The Borderlands a 10/10

It's repetitive, linear, grindy, and there's no exploration or story at all.
Think of it as a twin-stick arena. Each stage is a small area full of randomized traps and breakables. Several waves of enemies appear at the entrances on the sides of the map and you kill them. Sometimes there are other random oddities, dungeons (side areas with loot), treasure chests, or zelda-style shops on the map that mix it up. A boss spawns after the last wave, and a big boss spawns its own private arena at the end of each act. As you might expect, each stage has slightly stronger enemies than the last. This formula repeats for the whole game and then you win!
You can level up, pick up tons of (mostly useless) loot, and dump lots of points into whatever stats you choose. In this sense, it feels a bit like Diablo or any number of its contemporaries or clones. There's a hardcore mode for people who like permadeath, and several difficulty levels which just kinda make the game take longer to beat (i.e. they're not very hard, just time consuming).
If you like this sort of thing, then you'll like this game.

This would be a very decent free-to-play online FPS, unfortunately it's plagued by several things.  First off, it's very pay-to-win—players with deep pockets buy the biggest and best guns to dominate the match(a handgun that can kill with one shot to the leg?  I think not.).  And even most of the items you CAN buy only last for a short amount of time, mostly not even for a whole day.  And the "free" Welcome Package?  Having to PURCHASE in-game currency to receive a set of items isn't free, it's a purchase bonus.  Call it what it is, don't sugarcoat it.
Then, there's the bugs.  Half the time I launch the game, it fails(not anything wrong on my end, I checked), and when I was able to play, several of my simple achievements(such as "Play as the Rifle Man for the first time") took several unnecessary playthroughs to unlock.  Oh, then there's the plagiarized Resident Evil art used in the promo pictures when you launch the game.  Shameful.
Honestly, this could've been a great, free alternative to CS:GO.  But when all is said and done, it's only worth playing for the initial 15+ minutes to unlock the Black Rose knife for a much better free-to-play online FPS—Team Fortress 2.
